Saatvik SS-EPE UVT-F and SS-EPE UVC-B are
highly transparent encapsulant films with
excellent weather resistance, strong adhesion
to glass and metal materials, and outstanding
operational performance. These films enable
shorter lamination cycles while maintaining
high module efficiency.
The EPE-series provides a highly cost-effective
encapsulant solution for PID-free requirements
in both P-type and N-type bifacial PV modules.
It can successfully withstand a 288-hour PID
test under test conditions of 85°C, 85% RH, and
1500 VDC. In addition, EPE-series films exhibit
excellent long-term durability and reliability.

Precaution:
• Film should not be exposed to the atmosphere for a long time. Significant exposure will cause a decrease in functionality.
• Store in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated place. Keep away from heat and sunlight, and keep away from active oxidizing materials.
• Avoid making contact with bare hands, water, oil, organic solvents and other chemicals
Storage conditions:
1. The product shall be stored indoors at temperature between 0°C and 30°C, and humidity below 60% RH.
2. Avoiding direct sunshine, and keeping away from heat and dust.
3. Shelf life of SS-EPE UVT-F & SS-EPE UVC-B products is 5 months from the production date.
4. Use up within 6 hours after opening.
Notes:
1. When preparing gel content samples, the sample preparation structure should be stacked according to the BOM of the actual PV modules.
2. For P-type or N-type PV modules, SS-EPE UVT-F is recommended as the encapsulant for glass - to - glass module configurations.
3. For P-type or N-type PV modules, SS-EPE UVT-F and SS-EPE UVC-B films are recommended as encapsulant for glass - to - transparent backsheet module configurations.
4. Test condition: 85°C, 85%RH, 1500Vdc, and 288h.

Bonded Labour and
Abolition Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness:
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
Saatvik Group (“Saatvik”) is committed to upholding the highest ethical standards in all
aspects of its operations. We recognize that bonded labour, a form of forced labour, is a
grave violation of human rights and an illegal practice that undermines human dignity.
Bonded labour occurs when individuals are forced to work to repay a debt and are
trapped in exploitative conditions with no freedom to leave.
This Bonded Labour and Abolition Policy (“Policy”) outlines our zero -tolerance stance
towards bonded labour within Saatvik and across our supply chains. It sets out
measures to prevent, identify, and eliminate any form of bonded labour, ensuring
compliance with national laws and international labour standards.
2. Objective
2.1. To eradicate bonded labour in all forms.
2.2. To enforce existing laws and introduce new legislative measures where necessary
to prevent bonded labour.
2.3. To provide relief, rehabilitation, and reintegration services to victims of bonded
labour.
2.4. To create awareness about the illegality and harmful effects of bonded labour
among employers/suppliers, workers, and the general public.
2.5. To encourage fair wages, decent work conditions, and protection of labour rights.
3. Scope of the Policy
This Policy, titled “Bonded Labour and Abolition Policy” (“Policy”), is applicable across
operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to
as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff,
trainees, probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers,
agents, business partners, and any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or
indirectly.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4. Policy Commitments
Saatvik is committed to:
4.1. Preventing the use of bonded or forced labour in any form.
4.2. Promoting fair and ethical employment practices across its operations and
supply chains.
4.3. Ensuring transparency, accountability, and responsibility in labour practices.
5. Legal and Regulatory Compliance
Saatvik strictly adheres to all national laws prohibiting bonded labour and is committed
to the principles outlined in:
5.1. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
5.2. International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions, particularly those related to
forced labour.
5.3. Relevant national labour laws in the countries where we operate.
In cases of non -compliance, immediate corrective actions will be taken, and legal
consequences will follow as per applicable laws.
6. Prohibition of Bonded Labour
Saatvik explicitly prohibits the use of bonded labour in any form. No employee,
contractor, or worker in our supply chain shall be required to work to repay a debt under
coercive or exploitative conditions.
7. Recruitment and Employment Practices
All workers, whether directly employed by Saatvik or engaged through third -party
contractors, must be employed under free and fair conditions. No employment contract
should involve unreasonable deductions, advance payments, or loan arrangements
that lead to debt bondage.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Saatvik follows the Employer Pays Principle, that is, r ecruitment fees are borne by the
employer, not the employee. Any recruitment-related fees imposed on workers are
strictly prohibited.
8. Freedom of Movement
All workers have the freedom to leave their employment or terminate their contracts at
any time, subject to reasonable notice and Saatvik’s policies.
Confiscation, destruction, concealment, or retention of personal documents (such as
passports, government -issued identification, or work permits) is strictly prohibited,
except where temporary retention is required by law for administrative or immigration
processing.
9. Supplier and Contractor Responsibility
9.1. Supplier Code of Conduct
All suppliers, subcontractors, and business partners must comply with Saatvik’s
Supplier Code of Conduct, which includes specific provisions on prohibiting
bonded labour.
Suppliers are required to maintain fair and transparent working conditions and
ensure that workers are not subject to debt bondage or forced labour conditions.
9.2. Auditing and Monitoring
Regular audits and assessments will be conducted to ensure compliance with
this Policy across our supply chain. Any suppliers found to be using bonded
labour will be required to take immediate corrective action or face termination of
contracts.
9.3. Training and Capacity Building :
Saatvik shall provide training to suppliers and contractors on the ethical
recruitment of workers and the prevention of bonded labour.
Capacity-building programmes will be implemented to raise awareness of labour
rights and improve working conditions across the supply chain.

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
10. Reporting and Grievance Mechanism
10.1. Reporting of Violations :
Employees, contractors, and third -party workers are encouraged to report any
suspected instances of bonded labour through Saatvik’s confidential
whistleblower system , as outlined in Saatvik’s Whistle Blower Policy and Vigil
Mechanism or Grievance Redress al Mechanism for internal and external
stakeholders.
Reports can be made anonymously, and Saatvik guarantees protection from
retaliation for individuals who report concerns in good faith.
10.2. Investigation and Remediation :
Any reported violation of this Policy will be thoroughly investigated by Saatvik. If
bonded labour is discovered, immediate corrective action will be taken to
address the situation and provide support to affected workers.
This may include the provision of financial support, legal assistance, and
alternative employment opportunities for the affected individuals.
11. Employee Training and Awareness
All employees of Saatvik will receive regular training on this Policy and the importance
of eradicating bonded labour. This includes training on how to recognize signs of bonded
labour and the procedures for reporting any concerns.
Managers and supervisors will receive additional training to ensure they can effectively
implement and monitor compliance with this Policy.
12. Continuous Improvement and Monitoring
Saatvik shall monitor the effectiveness of this Policy through measurable indicators,
including but not limited to:
• Percentage of high-risk suppliers screened and/or audited.
• Number of findings related to forced/bonded labour and percentage resolved
through corrective action plans.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Number of grievances received and remediation outcomes.
• Training coverage for internal teams and suppliers in high -risk regions.
Performance against these indicators will inform Saatvik’s annual improvement plans
and be reviewed by relevant governance bodies.
13. Quantitative Commitments
13.1 Conduct periodic audits covering at least 50% of high -risk suppliers by 2030 to
ensure they are free from forced labour practices, with a plan to gradually expand
coverage in subsequent years.
13.2 Ensure zero tolerance for forced labour across Saatvik’s own operations
immediately and extend compliance requirements to all direct suppliers by 2026.
14. Employees’ Duties
Each employee of Saatvik has a duty to comply with the provisions of this Policy. If any
employee of Saatvik has knowledge or reasonable suspicion of the use of forced or
bonded labour in Saatvik’s operations or value chain, he/she shall immediately report
this to his/her Human Resource Head, through Whistle Blower mechanism or Grievance
Redressal Mechanism for internal stakeholders.
15. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder
expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made i n
writing and will become effective upon approval by ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The Human Resources Department of Saatvik
is the final authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy.
Saatvik reserves the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

title: Code of Ethics and Conduct Policy

pages.text:
Code of Ethics and Conduct
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting held on
11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or replaced by the
Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
2
1. Prologue
Saatvik Group (“Saatvik”) aim to be the industry leader by achieving excellence in everything it
does, including standards of business conduct. This objective shall be achieved by adopting a
policy to conduct its business with responsibility, integrity, fairness, transparency, and honesty.
The purpose of this Code of Ethics and Conduct (“Code” or “Code of Conduct”) is to promote
conduct of business ethically in an efficient and transparent manner and to meet its
obligations to shareholders and all other stakeholders. This Code is also a tool in carrying out
the Saatvik’s social responsibility in a more effective manner. This Code sets out a broad policy
for one’s conduct in dealing with Saatvik, fellow directors and employees, and the external
environment in which Saatvik operates.
2. Scope and Applicability of this Code
2.1. This Code of Conduct applies across operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and
its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”). The Policy
applies to all employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff, trainees,
probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers, agents,
business partners, and any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or indirectly,
to ensure compliance with the highest standards of corporate governance and
regulatory requirements.
2.2. For the purpose of this Code of Conduct:
“Board” means the Board of Directors of Saatvik;
“Employee” means every person in a permanent or temporary role at Saatvik at its
various business locations;
“Director” means a member of the Board;
2.3. Where Saatvik is a major or strategic shareholder in another company, that company
should also be made aware of this Code and encouraged to have a similar Code.
2.4. We aim to choose people with high moral and ethical values compatible with our own
as our business partners. If we find ourselves in a business relationship with anyone

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
3
(e.g. distributor, agent, joint venture partner, supplier, etc.) where it is clear that there is
a serious incompatibility that cannot be resolved, we will seek to terminate the
relationship.
3. Regulatory Compliance
Saatvik is committed to high standards of corporate governance and believes in compliance
with all the laws and regulations both in letter and spirit. Saatvik has endeavoured to set
standards for itself, which are ahead of the times and higher than those stipulated by law.
Saatvik is committed to providing on time, accurate, and complete information as required, to
all concerned, including its stakeholders.
4. Respect for Individual
Saatvik's vision is based on inspiring and unleashing creative potential in the human assets of
Saatvik. This is possible in an environment where we all respect the rights of those around us.
In this direction, Saatvik shall:
4.1. Treat individuals in all aspects of employment solely on the basis of ability, irrespective
of race, caste, creed, religion, age, disability, gender, sexual orientation, or marital
status; and
4.2. Not tolerate racial, sexual, or any other kind of harassment.
5. Honest and Ethical Conduct
The Directors and Employees of Saatvik should act in accordance with the highest standards
of personal and professional integrity, honesty, and ethical conduct. Honest conduct is
conduct that is free from any fraud or deception. Ethical conduct is conduct conforming to
accepted professional standards of conduct and shall include ethical handling of actual or
apparent conflicts of interest between personal and professional relationships.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4
6. Conflict of Interest
The Directors and Employees shall not engage in any activity or enter into any pecuniary
relationship which might result in a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly.
A “conflict of interest” occurs when an individual’s personal interest directly or indirectly
interferes with or appears to interfere with the interest of Saatvik. The Directors and Employees
must act at all times in Saatvik’s best interest and avoid putting themselves in a position where
their personal interest conflicts or appears to conflict with the interest of Saatvik. Their
personal interest will also include those of their immediate relatives. Any Director or other
Employee who is aware of a conflict of interest or is concerned that a conflict might develop
is required to disclose the matter promptly to the Board in the case of a Director and to the
Managing Director in the case of any other Employee.
7. Misuse of Opportunities and Information
The Directors and Employees owe a duty to Saatvik to advance Saatvik’s business interest
when appropriate. The Directors and Employees are prohibited from taking (or directing to a
third party) a business opportunity (relevant to the line of business intended to be pursued by
the Saatvik) that is discovered through the use of Saatvik’s property, information, or position,
unless Saatvik has already been offered the opportunity and turned it down. The Directors and
Employees are prohibited from using Saatvik’s property, information, or position for personal
gain and from competing with Saatvik. Wherever, it is difficult to differentiate between personal
and Saatvik’s benefits or there are both personal and Saatvik’s benefits in certain activities, the
only prudent course of conduct for the Directors and Employees is to make sure that any use
of Saatvik’s property or services or such transaction that is not solely for the benefit of the
Saatvik has prior approval of the competent authority.
8. Confidential Information
During the course of employment or dealing with Saatvik, any information of a confidential
nature (whether about Saatvik, other companies or individuals) that is known to Directors or
Employees shall be treated as confidential unless publicly available. Such information should
be used only for the purpose of the business of Saatvik. The use of Saatvik’s information for

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
5
personal gain is strictly prohibited. This obligation continues for two years after leaving Saatvik.
Saatvik also respects the rights of others regarding their confidential information. Where
information is received from third parties under conditions of confidentiality, the Directors and
Employees shall comply with those conditions, but no one should solicit confidential
information from third parties without prior authorisation.
G. Fair Dealing
Saatvik does not seek competitive advantages through illegal or unethical business practices.
Each Director and Employee should endeavour to deal fairly with Saatvik’s customers, service
providers, suppliers, competitors, and other Employees. No Director or Employee should take
advantage of anyone through manipulation, concealment, abuse of privileged information,
misrepresentation of material facts, or any unfair dealing practice. The Directors and
Employees shall immediately bring to the notice of the Board and/or Managing Director, as
applicable, any unethical behaviour and actual or suspected fraud.
10. Protection and Proper Use of Saatvik’s Assets
The assets of Saatvik shall not be misused by the Directors and Employees during the course
of conducting the business of Saatvik or otherwise. The assets include tangible assets such as
equipment and machinery, systems, facilities, materials, resources, etc., as well as intangible
assets such as patents, proprietary information, process, design, etc., whether patented or
not, relationships with customers and suppliers, etc.
11. Bribery s Corruption
11.1 Procedure s Guideline
11.1.1 Bribery s Corruption involves the offering, making, requesting, or receiving payments
or payments in kind (gifts, favours, etc.) to induce people to act illegally or dishonestly
or to provide a benefit that is not legitimately due, and in that way, corrupt the decision-
making process.
11.1.2 Under no circumstances will Saatvik approve any offers, making, requesting or
receiving irregular payments or payments in kind to win business or influence a

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
6
business decision in our favour, or which have the intention of a function being
performed improperly.
11.1.3 Offers to and the making of bribes, ‘kick -backs’, secret commissions and similar
payments are strictly prohibited. Moreover, they may expose our Company s relevant
parties to criminal prosecution and serious penalties under laws of the operating
country, as well as those of the country in question.
11.1.4 Saatvik is committed to prohibiting bribery and corruption in all of its business dealings.
Bribery and corruption risks occur in three key areas, namely (1). Facilitation Payments
(2). Gifts and Hospitality (3). Dealing with third parties s intermediaries.
11.1.5 This policy sets out Saatvik’s approach in each of the above three key areas, provides
information and guidance on recognising and dealing with bribery and corruption issues
and outlines the steps the Company takes to implement and monitor bribery and
corruption risks.
11.1.6 It is important that the Company's expectations are clearly communicated and
accepted by the aforementioned parties.
11.2 Facilitation Payments s Rules
11.2.1 Facilitation payments are relatively minor payments, more by way of a token, made to
lower-level officials or Government Employees. These payments are sought to
expedite routine services or administrative actions provided or performed by those
individuals.
11.2.2 In general, facilitation payments differ from bribes in that the purpose of the facilitation
payment is to expedite the completion of a routine service or administrative action
which the Company is entitled to under local law and in the ordinary course of events.
The payment is not an attempt to distort a proper decision-making process.
11.2.3 The Company opposes to make any facilitation payments as a matter of policy, and
every effort should be made to resist them. An understanding of what lies behind a
request (e.g., the person may be seeking recognition or status) may suggest ways to
meet the request in an acceptable way.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
7
11.2.4 The Company recognises that in some countries, it may be possible to make minor
facilitating payments. In other countries, however, strict legislation exists prohibiting
facilitation payments of any kind. Such legislation can have extra -territorial reach and
can therefore apply to any acts occurring outside the country in which the legislation is
made accordingly, no facilitation payments of any amount can be made unless the prior
consent and approval of the following persons within the Company has been obtained:
(1) Managing Director, (2) CEO.
11.2.5 When seeking approval, one should confirm that each of the following applies: The
purpose of the payment is to expedite the completion of a routine service or
administrative action, which the Company is entitled to under local law and in the
ordinary course of events. The payment must not be an attempt to distort a proper
decision-making process.
11.2.6 There is no reasonable alternative to making the payment. The business consequences
of not making the payment will be serious. The type and amount of the payment is
consistent with what is customarily sought, made, and sanctioned in the country
concerned.
11.2.7 The payment will not expose the Company and related parties to legal action under any
applicable law or regulation, as Management is aware of the payment, and the payment
is accounted for clearly s accurately.
11.2.8 Clear s accurate records of any facilitation payments approved under this policy
should be kept, detailing. The circumstances (conduct) under which the payment was
made. The value of the benefit. The date on which the conduct occurred. The identity
of the foreign public official or other person the payment was made. Particulars of the
routine government action that was sought, and the officer’s signature or some other
means of verifying their identity.
11.3 Gifts s Hospitality Rules
The Company and representatives must exercise caution regarding the giving or receiving of
business-related gifts or hospitality. Gifts can include direct payments, payments in kind such
as goods or services, travel and/or accommodation, entertainment, meals, personal favours,
etc.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8
11.3.1 Our Company recognises that in some countries the accepting or offering of gifts of
moderate value is in accordance with local business practice (i.e., where it is
customary to exchange gifts or gifts are appropriate for the occasion).
11.3.2 The local customs, monetary value of the gift, and legal requirements should be
considered when establishing whether a gift should be retained by the Company
representative, handed to the company or returned.
11.3.3 The policy and procedures below in relation to gifts and hospitality apply not only to
Company representatives but also to their immediate family members (spouse,
children, parents).
11.3.4 Certain gifts, regardless of value, must never be accepted, including cash, cash
equivalents (gift cards), loans, political contributions, drugs or other controlled
substances, discounts for product or services that are not available to others, personal
use of accommodation or transportation, and payments or loans to be used to
purchase personal property.
11.3.5 Our Company representatives must also not offer, give, request or accept gifts of any
kind in circumstances that could be considered as unduly influencing the party involved
or creating any business obligation or which has the intention of a function being
performed improperly.
11.3.6 Our Company representative (s) uncertain of any situation, it should be referred to
management for consideration. Additionally, any representative should not solicit gifts
or hospitality from a supplier, customer or other party with whom our Company
conducts business, nor should he or she exchange gifts with representatives from
competitors, as such actions may create a conflict of interest.
11.3.7 When the company is negotiating or considering contracts, the Company
representatives (s) should exercise particular caution in relation to any offers of
hospitality, entertainment or gifts. Our Company representatives who are in a position
of direct or indirect influence on the outcome of a negotiation should ensure that there
is no potential improper connection between any gift or hospitality and the business
opportunity in question. Gifts of any significance should be discussed with
management to avoid any suggestion of a conflict of interest.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
9
11.3.8 If any representative accepts or offers a gift or hospitality above INR 3,000 value to a
third party, the representative must declare the amount and nature of the gift or
hospitality; and the date the gift is offered or received or the hospitality incurred, to the
company Chief Financial Officer or a delegate appointed by the Chief Financial Officer.
The Company Chief Financial Officer or his or her delegate will record and maintain a
Gift and Hospitality Register.
11.4 Dealing with Third Parties s Intermediaries
11.4.1 One of the ways in which bribery s corruption can occur indirectly is through agents,
business partners and acquisitions.
11.4.2 Our Company could be held liable if it knew about, or deliberately ignored, the activities
of such third parties and leads to Risk of Bribery and Corruption.
11.4.3 Prior to dealing with third parties and intermediaries, business groups are responsible
for deciding the degree and manner of due diligence required to ascertain the bribery
and corruption risks of these parties. Business units must perform risk -based anti -
corruption due diligence, including:
• Verification of ownership, financial stability, and compliance history.
• Assessment of alignment with Saatvik’s Code of Conduct and Anti-Bribery Policy.
• Collection of supporting documents, such as contracts, questionnaires, and
certifications.
• Conducting anti-bribery questionnaires, compliance certifications, and background
checks.
11.4.4 To support due diligence, the following standards and records must be maintained:
• Standard due diligence procedures and work instructions on conducting the due
diligence exercise.
• Detailed records of due diligence program implementation.
• Document guidelines to ensure all steps and findings are clearly captured.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
10
• Evidence demonstrating detailed and concrete steps to investigate third parties
(suppliers, vendors, commission agents, brokers, sales representatives, distributors,
contractors, customs brokers, consultants) to ensure anti-corruption compliance and
prevent third-party corruption incidents.
• The program should demonstrate at least two of the following: evidence of a risk-based
approach, collection of data on third parties, benchmarking or other results.
11.4.5 Business groups are also responsible for conducting regular periodic reviews of the
anti-bribery risk of all arrangements with an agent, contractor, distributor and partner,
as appropriate. A review should also be conducted whenever any warning signs appear.
11.4.6 All business groups are responsible for maintaining clear records of the initial due
diligence performed and the subsequent reviews.
11.5 Lobbying and Political Contributions
11.5.1 The Company does not engage in any lobbying activities, political contributions or
charitable donations intended to obtain an improper advantage. All interactions with
public officials or government bodies must be transparent, compliant with applicable
laws, and conducted in accordance with Saatvik’s Code of Conduct and Anti -Bribery s
Anti-Corruption Policy.
11.5.2 All charitable donations must be approved by the CEO and documented, ensuring no
link to business inducements.
11.6 Implementation s Monitoring
11.6.1 To implement anti -bribery measures and monitor the occurrence of bribery and
corruption. This policy shall be supplemented by the company whistleblower policy
and redressal mechanism.
11.6.2 Bribery and corruption risks are addressed through this policy. The Company also
maintains a Whistleblower Policy.
11.6.3 Periodic risk assessments are made to identify bribery and corruption risk. Any risks
identified are investigated and followed up with controls tailored to manage the risks.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
11
11.6.4 We promote awareness s compliance of anti-bribery s corruption measures through,
appropriate dissemination of this policy. Publishing this policy on our Company
website, and requiring representatives to complete training on anti -bribery and
corruption where appropriate.
11.6.5 If you are unsure whether a particular act constitutes bribery or corruption or if you
believe a decision or action may be inconsistent with this policy or if you have any
queries, you should raise the issue promptly with your line manager.
11.6.6 If you feel unable to do the above, there are a number of other ways to raise a question
or concern. You can contact - The next level management. The Human Resources,
Legal or Group Audit Services representative of the company, or the Whistleblower
service.
11.6.7 Annual training on anti -bribery and corruption is mandatory for 100% of employees.
Training completion will be tracked in the HR Learning Management System.
11.6.8 Periodic independent audits of compliance with this policy shall be conducted.
Findings will be reported to the Board of Directors and relevant management
committees.
11.7 Commitments
11.7.1 Ensure 100% of employees receive annual training on anti -bribery and corruption.
Training completion will be tracked in the HR Learning Management System.
11.8 Reporting Violations s Whistle -blower Mechanism
Employees and third parties are encouraged to report any suspected bribery, corruption, or
unethical behaviour at lalit.singh@saatvikgroup.com. Retaliation against whistleblowers is
strictly prohibited. All reports will be treated confidentially and investigated promptly.
12. Money Laundering
Saatvik aims to:
• To prevent, detect, and report any instance of money laundering or suspicious
financial activity within Saatvik’s operations.

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
12
• To ensure compliance with all applicable Anti-Money Laundering (AML) laws, rules,
and regulations in India and other jurisdictions where Saatvik operates.
• To promote a culture of transparency and accountability across all financial
transactions and business relationships.
12.1 Anti-Money Laundering Commitments
Saatvik is committed to preventing money laundering and complying with all applicable anti-
money laundering (AML) regulations.
12.1.1 Saatvik shall not knowingly engage in or facilitate any activity involving the
concealment or conversion of illicit funds.
12.1.2 Saatvik shall establish due diligence procedures for all financial transactions and
ensure customer and third-party verification before initiating business relationships.
12.1.3 Saatvik shall monitor transactions to identify and report any signs or indicators of
money laundering.
12.1.4 Saatvik shall report all suspicious financial activities or instances where business
partners refuse to provide the required identity or transaction information.
12.1.5 Saatvik shall take appropriate legal action and cooperate with relevant authorities
and compliance departments to investigate and address violations involving fraud,
money laundering, or corruption.
12.1.6 Saatvik aims to:
• Conduct annual AML training for all employees and workers in FY 2026 to FY 2027.
• Undertake annual AML compliance audits across all financial transactions and
business units by FY 2027.
12.2 AML Training s Awareness
Saatvik shall provide periodic training and awareness programs on AML regulations, warning
signs, and reporting procedures for all employees involved in financial transactions, vendor
management, or compliance activities. Refresher sessions shall be held periodically to
ensure continued understanding and compliance across the organisation.
12.3 Reporting s Grievance Mechanism

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
13
Saatvik encourages all employees, suppliers, and partners to promptly report any suspected
or actual incident of money laundering, financial irregularity, or unethical conduct. Reports
may be made anonymously or with disclosure at lalit.singh@saatvikgroup.com. Saatvik shall
ensure that every concern raised is acknowledged, addressed, and documented in a fair and
transparent manner.
Retaliation against any person who raises a genuine concern in good faith is strictly
prohibited.
Verified cases of money laundering or related misconduct will be escalated to law
enforcement authorities and may result in disciplinary or legal action.
12.4 Roles s Responsibilities
Saatvik’s Finance Department shall implement and monitor AML controls, including
transaction verification and documentation. The Compliance Department shall oversee
policy execution, conduct training, and ensure all reports of suspicious activity are reviewed
and escalated appropriately. The Internal Audit Team shall perform independent AML
compliance reviews. All employees, contractors, and third parties are obligated to report
suspicious or irregular activities immediately to the Compliance Officer.
13. Wealth Creation
The Directors and Employees shall be committed to enhancing the shareholders’ worth/ value
and shall strictly comply with all regulations and laws that govern shareholders’ rights. The
Board shall duly and fairly inform the shareholders of all relevant aspects of Saatvik’s business
and disclose such information as may be required, from time to time, in accordance with the
applicable rules and regulations.
14. Safety, Health, and Environment
Saatvik’s vision envisages no compromise in its commitment to safety, health, and responsible
care for the environment. The health and safety of the people in and around its area of
operations are of paramount importance to Saatvik. Saatvik is committed to environmental

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
14
protection, pollution control, and maintenance of ecological balance. Saatvik shall maintain
high standards of pollution control, environmental protection and safety.
15. Adherence to Code
Adherence to this Code is a condition of employment with Saatvik. Violation of this Code shall
be treated as a serious matter and shall result in disciplinary action by the management. In
case there is any non -adherence, the employees shall report to the Reporting Authority, in
either of the following 2 ways:
15.1. By reporting on a separate E Mail ID: lalit.singh@saatvikgroup.com, which has been
created for reporting any violations or deviations. Emails sent to this E Mail ID shall be
directly delivered to the CHRO of Saatvik.
15.2. By reporting to the following executives: CEO, COO, Company Secretary and CFO.
Whilst reporting a non -adherence or a violation, the employees shall provide the
following information to the Management:
• The specific aspects of this Code which have been violated.
• The individual, group of people, or functions involved.
• A comprehensive description of the violation, giving details of the incident,
which will enable the management to understand the violation.
• Information/data that the employee has with him/her that management can
refer to, whilst investigating the violation.
• Employees reporting with mala fide or malicious intent or with a hidden agenda
shall also be considered as a violation of this adherence Code, except genuinely
mistaken reporting, based on evidence which could have been the subject
matter of varying interpretations. If the management, after investigation, finds
out that the reporting was mala fide or malicious, then the employee can expect
a serious management response.
• Anonymous reports will be accepted and investigated in good faith. Saatvik
strictly prohibits retaliation against any employee, supplier, or third party who
reports a concern honestly, whether anonymously or not. The identity of an

Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
15
employee reporting a violation shall be kept confidential, except if required to be
disclosed by law.
• After proper investigation, Saatvik shall respond to reported violations by taking
appropriate actions against the erring employee, like counselling, coaching,
performance-related actions, termination, as well as legal actions, depending
upon the seriousness and the organizational impact of the violation. In order to
maintain the dignity of an employee, actions taken by the management shall not
be publicised.
16. Review and Amendments
This Code shall be reviewed periodically, or in the event of significant regulatory or operational
changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder expectations, and
legal requirements. Any amendments to this Code shall be made in writing and will become
effective upon approval by the ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The Human Resources Department of Saatvik
is the final authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy.
Saatvik reserves the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

title: Community Engagement and Social Impact Policy

pages.text:
Community Engagement
and Social Impact Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
Saatvik Group envisions growth that is inclusive, equitable, and sustainable. This policy
defines the Saatvik’s approach to engaging with communities surrounding its
operational areas, with the objective of creating enduring social value s. It establishes
the foundation for how Saatvik builds meaningful relationships, identifies community
needs, and drives positive social impact through structured, participatory, and
responsible engagement practices .
2. Scope of the Policy
This policy titled, “ Community Engagement and Social Impact Policy” ( “Policy”), is
applicable across operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries
(collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”). The policy covers initiatives
implemented directly or through registered NGOs, trusts, or other entities associated
with Saatvik. The Policy also extends to contractors, suppliers, business partners, and
other third parties operating in or near community a reas, ensuring responsible conduct
and adherence to Saatvik’s social performance standards.
3. Policy Commitments
Saatvik is committed to:
3.1 Inclusivity: Engaging with diverse, marginali sed, and vulnerable groups to
ensure equitable participation and representation.
3.2 Participation: Enabling active involvement of communities in the planning,
implementation, and evaluation of program mes to ensure local relevance and
ownership.
3.3 Transparency: Upholding accountability and openness in communication,
decision-making, and reporting of engagement outcomes.
3.4 Partnership: Working collaboratively with local authorities, NGOs, community -
based organi sations, and social enterprises to enhance reach and maximi se
social impact.
3.5 Sustainability: Designing initiatives that create lasting value, strengthen
community resilience, and align with the United Nations Sustainable
Development Goals (SDGs).
3.6 Respect for Community Rights and Consent : Upholding the principles of Free,
Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) for projects that may impact local or

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Indigenous communities, in line with recognised international standards and
best practices.
4. Approach to Community Engagement and Social Impact
Assessment
4.1 The community engagement process shall include:
• Community Needs Assessment : Engage with local stakeholders to identify
socio-economic and environmental priorities using participatory tools,
consultations, and baseline surveys.
• Planning and Design : Develop engagement plans that align community
needs with Saatvik’s sustainability vision, ensuring that initiatives are
evidence-based, inclusive, and outcome -oriented.
• Implementation : Execute initiatives directly or through credible partners,
upholding ethical practices, inclusivity, and compliance with applicable
statutory and regulatory requirements.
• Monitoring, Evaluation, and Feedback : Track progress through defined
performance indicators, and periodic reviews. Establish feedback
mechanisms to incorporate community perspectives and enhance
programme effectiveness.
• Communication and Reporting : Maintain transparent communication with
stakeholders through regular reporting, community outreach, and an
accessible grievance redressal mechanism.
4.2 Saatvik shall undertake Social Impact Assessments (SIA) for projects involving
land acquisition or significant land -use changes, in accordance with the Right to
Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and
Resettlement (RFCTLA RR) Act, 2013. The SIA shall:
• Evaluate potential social, economic, and cultural impacts on affected
communities.
• Identify measures to mitigate negative effects and strengthen positive
outcomes.
• Involve consultations with affected stakeholders to ensure inclusiveness and
transparency.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Be conducted by independent expert agencies to ensure objectivity and
regulatory compliance.
• Produce actionable recommendations for project design, implementation,
and rehabilitation measures.
• Disclose findings publicly in line with statutory requirements and share them
with affected communities.
• Monitor post -implementation outcomes to assess the effectiveness of
mitigation measures and ensure sustained community well -being.
5. Roles and Responsibilities
5.1 Executive Management: Provide leadership, ensure alignment with this policy,
and allocate necessary resources.
5.2 Sustainability, CSR and HR Department: Plan, execute, and monitor engagement
initiatives and maintain communication with stakeholders.
5.3 Project Managers: Integrate community perspectives and impact mitigation
measures into operational planning.
6. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder
expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made i n
writing and will become effective upon approval by ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The HR and CSR departments of
Saatvik are the final authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned
in the Policy. Saatvik reserves the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

Conﬂict Minerals &
Responsible Minerals
Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and EƯectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is eƯective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik
Group” or “Saatvik”) are committed to conducting business responsibly, ethically, and
in alignment with the highest standards of sustainability and human rights. As a solar PV
module manufacturer operating in global supply chains, Saatvik recognizes that its
products/raw materials may contain 3TG and hence, will ensure that minerals used in
its products do not directly or indirectly ﬁnance armed conﬂict, human rights abuses,
or environmental harm.
This Conﬂict Minerals & Responsible Minerals Policy (“Policy”) establishes Saatvik’s
commitment, principles, and expectations related to the responsible sourcing of
minerals, particularly those originating from conﬂict-a Ưected and high-risk areas.
2. Objective
The Purpose of this policy is to:
2.1. Prevent the use of minerals that directly or indirectly ﬁnance armed groups or
contribute to human rights abuses.
2.2. Ensure responsible sourcing of minerals used in Saatvik’s products in alignment
with international regulations and standards.
2.3. Embed conﬂict minerals due diligence into Saatvik’s sustainable procurement
and supplier governance framework.
2.4. Set clear expectations for suppliers regarding transparency, traceability, and
responsible mineral sourcing.
3. Scope and Applicability
This Policy shall be read in conjunction with s Saatvik’s ESG Policy, Supplier Code of
Conduct, and Sustainable Procurement Policy.
By signing or otherwise committing to comply with Saatvik’s Supplier Code of
Conduct, suppliers automatically agree to adhere to the requirements of this Conﬂict

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Minerals & Responsible Minerals Policy, including all obligations related to responsible
sourcing, due diligence, transparency, and cooperation.
Compliance with this Policy is a mandatory condition of doing business with Saatvik
and forms an integral part of Saatvik’s supplier governance framework. This policy
applies to:
 Saatvik Green Energy Limited and all its subsidiaries.
 All employees, directors, oƯicers, and relevant functions, particularly
Procurement, Supply Chain, Quality, and Sustainability.
 All suppliers, contractors, and business partners involved in the supply of raw
materials, components, or products that may contain covered minerals.
This Policy covers the entire supply chain, including upstream suppliers where
relevant.
4. Deﬁnitions
4.1. Conﬂict Minerals / Covered Minerals : Minerals deﬁned as tin, tantalum,
tungsten, and gold (3TG), their ores and derivatives, as well as other minerals
such as cobalt and mica where relevant, that are sourced from conﬂict-a Ưected
or high-risk areas.
4.2. Conﬂict-AƯected and High-Risk Areas (CAHRAs) : Regions a Ưected by armed
conﬂict, widespread violence, or human rights abuses, including but not limited
to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and its adjoining countries.
4.3. Responsible Sourcing : Sourcing minerals in a manner that respects human
rights, avoids ﬁnancing conﬂict, and complies with applicable laws and
international due diligence standards.
5. Regulatory and Framework Alignment
Saatvik aligns its approach to responsible mineral sourcing with the following:
 OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Supply Chains of Minerals
from Conﬂict-AƯected and High-Risk Areas
 Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Section 1502)

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
 EU Regulation 2017/821 on Responsible Mineral Sourcing
 UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
 Responsible Minerals Initiative (RMI)
 Saatvik ESG Policy, Supplier Code of Conduct, and Sustainable Procurement
Policy.
6. Policy Commitments
Saatvik commits to:
 Not knowingly sourcing conﬂict minerals from non-certiﬁed or non-
responsible sources that contribute to armed conﬂict or human rights
violations.
 All 3TG minerals procured shall originate only from recycled or scrap sources
(if applicable).
 Promoting transparency and traceability in mineral supply chains.
 Supporting the responsible sourcing of minerals, including from CAHRAs,
where sourced responsibly and in line with OECD guidance.
 Continuously improving its due diligence processes based on evolving
regulations and stakeholder expectations.
 Saatvik will ensure to provide trainings to 50% of its suppliers on conﬂict
mineral policy and supplier code of conduct by 2026.
 Saatvik will ask declaration of all its suppliers on conﬂict minerals by 2027 and
ensure complete compliance.
7. Supplier Expectations and Requirements
In line with Saatvik’s Supplier Code of Conduct, suppliers are required to comply with
this Conﬂict Minerals & Responsible Minerals Policy and demonstrate responsible
sourcing practices across their operations and supply chains.
 Signing and complying with the Supplier Code of Conduct shall be deemed as
conﬁrmation of the supplier’s commitment to this Policy, unless otherwise
communicated in writing by Saatvik.
 Establish their own conﬂict minerals or responsible minerals policies and due
diligence processes.

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
 Conduct reasonable due diligence on their supply chains in line with OECD
Guidance.
 Source minerals from smelters and reﬁners that are conformant or validated
under recognised programmes such as RMI (RMAP), LBMA, or RJC.
 Provide accurate, complete, and timely information on mineral sourcing upon
request, including conﬂict minerals declarations or templates where applicable.
 Cascade these requirements to their own suppliers.
Failure to meet these expectations may result in corrective action plans, business
restrictions, or disengagement.
8. Due Diligence Process
Saatvik follows a risk-based due diligence approach consistent with OECD Guidance:
 Establish strong management systems – Integration of responsible minerals
requirements into procurement, contracts, and supplier onboarding.
 Identify and assess risks – Identiﬁcation of materials and suppliers that may
involve covered minerals and assessment of sourcing risks.
 Design and implement risk response – Engagement with suppliers, corrective
action plans, and escalation where risks are identiﬁed.
 Independent veriﬁcation – Participation in or reliance on industry-recognised
assurance schemes and audits where applicable.
 Reporting and disclosure – Transparent communication to customers,
stakeholders, and through sustainability disclosures.
9. Sustainable Procurement
As part of Saatvik’s sustainable procurement framework, the Company:
 Integrates conﬂict minerals and responsible sourcing criteria into supplier
selection, evaluation, and retention.
 Requires critical suppliers to acknowledge and comply with Saatvik’s Supplier
Code of Conduct and this Policy.
 Conducts supplier ESG risk assessments, with conﬂict minerals considered a
key risk factor.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
 Engages suppliers through training, awareness, and improvement programmes
on responsible sourcing.
 Monitors supplier compliance through documentation reviews, self-
assessments, and audits where required.
 Maintains evidence of supplier declarations, corrective actions, and continuous
improvement for ESG ratings and customer assessments.
10. Roles and Responsibilities
 Board of Directors / ESG Council: Oversight and strategic direction on
responsible sourcing.
 Procurement & Supply Chain: Implementation of this Policy in sourcing,
contracting, and supplier management.
 Corporate Sustainability Team: Monitoring, reporting, and supplier
engagement.
 Suppliers: Compliance with this Policy and responsible sourcing expectations.
11. Training and Awareness
Saatvik shall provide appropriate training and awareness to relevant employees and
suppliers to ensure eƯective implementation of this Policy.
12. Reporting and Grievance Mechanism
Concerns related to conﬂict minerals or responsible sourcing may be reported through
mechanism established in supplier code of conduct i.e. ,
supplier_reporting@saatvikgroup.com ; All concerns will be reviewed and addressed in
a fair and conﬁdential manner.
Any non-compliance with this Policy shall be addressed in accordance with the
corrective action, audit, suspension, and disengagement mechanisms deﬁned in
Saatvik’s Supplier Code of Conduct and applicable supplier agreements.

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
13. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed periodically or in response to regulatory or operational
changes. Amendments shall be e Ưective upon approval by the ESG Council / Board of
Directors.
Disclaimer:
This Policy does not replace, or duplicate requirements set out in the Supplier Code of Conduct. Instead,
it provides detailed guidance and due diligence expectations speciﬁc to conﬂict minerals and responsible
mineral sourcing, in furtherance of the principles already established under the Supplier Code of
Conduct. Saatvik reserves the right to modify this Policy from time to time.

Data Privacy &
Protection Policy
Version 2.0
Approval and EƯectiveness
This Policy was initially issued on 2nd May 2025. The Policy was subsequently reviewed and revised (Version 2.0) and
approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited in its meeting held on 11th December 2025. The
revised Policy is eƯective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or replaced by the Board/ESG
Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 2.0
Policy Date: 2nd May 2025
Revision Date: 11th December 2025
1. Introduction
Saatvik has established a Data Privacy & Protection Policy which supports the strategic
aims of the business and is committed for maintaining and improving data security posture
within the organisation and minimizing its exposure to all risks.
When used properly, Information (data) helps companies to better understand the needs
and desires of their interested parties. It also forms the basis to automate the process that
help companies to evolve their operations. With the increasing use of digital platforms,
issues like data protection and privacy have become more prominent in the public eye. At
Saatvik Group (“Saatvik” , “We” , “Our”), we understand the concerns that can arise due to
mishandling of collected information that is personal in nature and are committed to
applying the highest standards of fairness, transparency, and accountability in managing
personal data.
Saatvik is committed to safeguarding the privacy and conﬁdentiality of any information
entrusted to its care. Saatvik is dedicated to upholding this fundamental responsibility by
ensuring the proper safeguarding and utilization of personal information, also known as
"Personal Data" , gathered by us.
2. Purpose
This policy's objective is to protect the personal information of current, former, and
potential workers, clients, and associates in relation to the gathering, use, and sharing of
personal data.
3. Scope
This policy is applicable to all personal data collected, stored, or processed across
operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the
“Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”), covering employees, job applicants, contractors,
consultants, vendors, suppliers, customers, digital users, and any third parties whose data
we process. The policy is applicable:
 irrespective of the form of its presentation or the medium used (paper, tape, ﬁlm,
electronic media etc.)
 irrespective of whose order, on whose behalf, or for whose account such information
is stored,
 regardless of how such knowledge is acquired (directly, through seeing, hearing, etc.,
or indirectly, through accessing a document that contains information, etc.).
 regardless of any other characteristic of such information, hereinafter referred to as
personal data.

3
Version: 2.0
Policy Date: 2nd May 2025
Revision Date: 11th December 2025
4. Deﬁnitions
S. No. Term Deﬁnition
1. Applicable Laws “Applicable Laws” shall mean and include all applicable
laws (including the DPDP Act, the IT Act, the IT Rules and
the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 and
such other similar laws / legislations which may be enacted
from time to time), statutes, legislative enactments,
ordinances, judgments, decrees, declarations, notiﬁcations,
guidelines, circulars, directives, codes, injunctions, writs,
rules, bye-laws, regulations, policies, directions, demands,
assessments, conventions, orders, interpretations,
licenses, permits, authorisations, standards and
requirements of all government authorities, and all
government approvals, whether in eƯect on the date of this
Privacy Policy or thereafter.
2. IT Act “IT Act” shall mean the Information Technology Act,
2000, of India and the rules prescribed thereunder, as
amended, substituted, modiﬁed or re-enacted from
time to time.
3. IT Rules “IT Rules” shall mean the Information Technology
(Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and
Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011, as
amended, substituted, modiﬁed or re-enacted from time to
time.
4. Data “Data” means a representation of information, facts,
concepts, opinions or instructions in a manner suitable for
communication, interpretation or processing by human
beings or by automated means.
5. Personal Data  Data which relates to an individual who can be
identiﬁed from that data; or
 Expression of opinion about an individual
 Personal data may include any personal details
such as name, address, telephone numbers,
email IDs, work experience information, health
records, PAN number, driving license number,
etc.

4
Version: 2.0
Policy Date: 2nd May 2025
Revision Date: 11th December 2025
S. No. Term Deﬁnition
6. Sensitive Personal
Data
 Any personal data that contains an opinion about a
person or may induce the formation of an opinion
that may negatively impact an individual personally
or professionally.
 Any personal data from which an implication of
criminal conduct can be drawn.
 Sensitive personal data includes all kinds of
national ID numbers, ﬁnancial data, religious
beliefs, political opinions, physical or mental
health conditions, sexual life, or any criminal

We use cookies to enable the Data Principal to make the best possible use of the website.

generating domain but also on other Saatvik’s websites. The requirement for the use of cross-
domain cookies is that they are used on websites within an application, and identical cookies

Environmental, Social &
Governance (ESG) Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
Saatvik Group (“Saatvik”) envisions a future where business growth goes hand in hand
with environmental responsibility, social responsibility, and governance. Saatvik
recognises that its operations have a direct and indirect influence on the ecosystem,
workforce, and communities it engages with. Hence, this Environmental, Social, and
Governance (ESG) Policy serves as a foundational document guiding Saatvik’s journey
towards sustainable excellence.
Our approach to sustainability is rooted in ethical business practices, innovation, and
accountability. Through this policy, we aim to integrate ESG considerations into every
business decision, process, and practice to create long-term value for stakeholders and
contribute to a resilient and inclusive future.
2. Objective
This ESG Policy aims to:
2.1. Establish a structured framework to embed ESG principles across Saatvik’s
operations and decision -making processes.
2.2. Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations, as well as adherence
to national and international sustainability frameworks.
2.3. Strengthen governance mechanisms that uphold transparency, integrity, and
accountability.
2.4. Promote sustainable resource management, reduce environmental impact, and
contribute towards climate action.
2.5. Encourage equity, and inclusion within the organi sation and empower
communities around our operational sites.
2.6. Facilitate continuous improvement in ESG performance through monitoring,
stakeholder engagement, and transparent disclosure.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
3. Scope of the Policy
This Policy, titled “Environmental, Social & Governance (ESG) Policy ” (“Policy”), is
applicable across operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries
(collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”). The Policy extends to all
employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff, trainees, probationers, and
temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers, agents, business partners, and
any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or indirectly along with all the
operations in the entire value chain of the Company. The Policy is applicable across all
operations and activities within Saatvik’s entire value chain.
4. Basic Principles and Governance
Saatvik acknowledges and aligns its practices with the principles outlined in the
following international standards:
4.1. Applicable local, national and international environmental and social (including
occupational health and safety) legislations
4.2. National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC)
4.3. Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)
4.4. United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDG’s)
4.5. United Nations Global Compact (UNGC)
4.6. United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGP)
4.7. Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB)
5. ESG Framework
5.1. In alignment with our ESG commitment, Saatvik has established a
comprehensive ESG Framework that provides structure and direction to our
sustainability initiatives. This framework is informed by international and national
standards, evolving legislation, i ndustry best practices, and the expectations of
our key stakeholders.
5.2. Our ESG Framework encompasses the identification of material topics across
Environmental, Social, and Governance pillars, ensuring all relevant risks,

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
opportunities, and priorities are addressed. These material topics guide our
performance disclosures, target-setting, and implementation strategies.
5.3. To effectively monitor and drive progress, we establish clear Key Performance
Indicators (KPIs) aligned with national and international frameworks. Through
regular due diligence, gap assessments, and benchmarking against best
practices, we ensure continuou s improvement and alignment with evolving ESG
standards.
5.4. Our ESG Framework serves as the cornerstone of our sustainability efforts,
unifying purpose and direction across the organi sation while shaping collective
ESG aspirations and actions.
6. Key Focus Areas
6.1. Environmental Responsibility
Saatvik is committed to minimi sing the environmental impact of its operations,
products, and services. We strive to prevent and reduce waste, emissions, and
discharges, while continuously improving the efficiency of natural resource
consumption. Through proactive risk management, we ide ntify and control
environmental hazards inherent in our activities. We aim to integrate
environmental responsibility into all aspects of our business management,
promoting the sustainable use of our products throughout their lifecycle, and
supporting customers in designing and manufacturing innovative, safe, and
reliable solutions.
• Renewable Energy Integration: Saatvik is committed to increasing the use
of renewable energy across its operations. We aim to reduce dependence on
non-renewable sources and target a 50% share of renewable energy by FY
2028. This includes adopting solar, wind, and other clean energy sol utions
wherever feasible.
• Emissions Management: Saatvik strives to prevent and minimi se emissions
and environmental discharges from our operations. We continuously
monitor, report, and improve processes to reduce our carbon footprint and
mitigate environmental hazards. We strive to invest in and adopt advanced
technologies, such as energy -efficient systems, low -emission equipment,

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
and smart process controls, to reduce emissions across our operations. We
aim to explore cleaner production methods and carbon reduction solutions
that support our transition to a low -carbon, sustainable business model .
Saatvik commits to minimising air pollution from its operations by adopting
cleaner technologies, preventive maintenance, process optimisation, and
compliance with applicable air emission standards.
Saatvik commits to achieving a minimum 1% Year-on-Year reduction in Scope
1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions intensity across its operations through energy
efficiency improvements, process optimisation, and increased use of
renewable energy.
• Circular Economy: We promote sustainable resource management by
integrating circular economy principles into our operations. This includes
reducing waste generation, reusing materials, and recycling end -of-life
products to minimise environmental impact.
Saatvik commits to achieving zero waste to landfill across its operations by
2030 through waste reduction, segregation, recycling, and responsible
disposal practices.
Saatvik commits to conducting a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) for at least one
product by FY 2026 to identify environmental impacts across the product
lifecycle and inform design and improvement decisions.
• Water Management: Saatvik shall manage water resources responsibly
across all operations, ensuring efficient use, conservation, and protection of
local water bodies. Saatvik shall monitor water consumption and discharge,
implement water-saving measures including recycling, reuse, and rainwater
harvesting, and treat effluents in compliance with applicable laws and
regulations. Periodic audits and risk assessments shall be conducted to
address water -related risks, particularly in high -stress regions. Employee s
and stakeholders shall be engaged to promote water stewardship and
sustainable water practices. Saatvik aims to achieve Zero Liquid Discharge
(ZLD) at its manufacturing facilities by optimising water us age, maximising
reuse and recycling, and ensuring no untreated effluent is discharged outside
operations.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Environmental services & advocacy: Saatvik promotes environmental
responsibility across its products by integrating sustainability considerations
into product design, manufacturing, use, and end -of-life stages. The
Company supports customers and stakeholders through responsible
product info rmation, compliance with environmental standards, and
promotion of energy-efficient and low-impact solutions.
Saatvik engages with industry platforms, suppliers, and communities to
encourage environmentally responsible practices, knowledge sharing, and
continuous improvement in product environmental performance.
• Biodiversity Conservation: Saatvik is committed to protecting biodiversity
by minimising impacts on local ecosystems, complying with applicable
environmental clearance requirements, and promoting greenbelt
development and nature -positive initiatives around its operational sites.
Saatvik undertakes environmental and biodiversity impact assessments,
obtain all statutory approvals, and integrate mitigation measures during
project planning, development, and operations to avoid, minimise, and
manage impacts on biodiversity for all existing and upcoming projects .
• Training & Awareness: We educate and train employees and contractors on
environmental responsibility, ensuring sustainable practices are embedded
in daily operations. Regular workshops, awareness campaigns, and capacity-
building programmes are conducted to enhance environmental stewardship
across all levels of the organisation. Our target is for 100% of employees to
undergo at least one mandatory environmental responsibility training
annually, with progress monitored and reported to ensure full participati on.
6.2. Social Responsibility
Saatvik recogni ses its responsibility towards society, employees, and
stakeholders, and seeks to contribute positively to sustainable development
while promoting human welfare, safety, and inclusivity. Our social responsibility
framework encompasses the following key area s:
• Human Rights: We uphold the highest standards of human rights across all
operations and business interactions. Saatvik is committed to preventing
human rights abuses and ensuring equality, dignity, and respect for all
individuals, including employees, contractors, suppl iers, and communities.

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
We actively promote fair labo ur practices, prohibit child and forced labo ur,
and support freedom of association and collective bargaining.
• Occupational Health and Safety: We implement robust occupational
health and safety management systems to minimise workplace risks, prevent
accidents, and maintain a safe and healthy work environment. Regular safety
audits, risk assessments, drills, and training program mes are conducted to
foster a culture of safety and well-being throughout the organi sation.
• Employee Engagement: We strive to foster an inclusive culture of open
communication, participation, and feedback. Employees are encouraged to
share ideas, contribute to decision -making processes, and participate in
initiatives that support Saatvik’s sustainability and social goals. Engagement
surveys, recognition program mes, and skill development initiatives are
conducted regularly to ensure high employee motivation and satisfaction.
• Non-Discrimination: Saatvik shall provide a workplace free from
discrimination, ensuring equal opportunities for all employees and
stakeholders irrespective of race, gender, age, religion, caste, disability,
sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law. S aatvik shall
implement fair employment practices, equitable treatment, and unbiased
decision-making in recruitment, compensation, promotion, training, and
other employment -related matters. Regular awareness program mes and
monitoring mech anisms shall be conducted to prevent discriminatory
behaviour and promote an inclusive and respectful work environment.
Saatvik aims to achieve 100% awareness among employees on non -
discrimination policies and practices by FY 2027.
• Safe Working Conditions: Saatvik is committed to providing workplaces that
are safe, secure, and conducive to productivity. Facilities are designed and
maintained to meet high safety standards, with regular inspections, hazard
assessments, and improvements to ensure that all empl oyees and
contractors work in a risk-free environment.
• Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: We strive to create a diverse and inclusive
workforce where all individuals have equal opportunities to thrive. Saatvik
promotes gender equality, cultural diversity, and equitable practices across
recruitment, development, and career progression. Inclusion is embedded in

8
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
our organi sational culture, ensuring that differences are respected and
valued.
• Empowering Communities: Saatvik engages with local communities
through initiatives that promote education, healthcare, livelihood
enhancement, and sustainable development. Our CSR programmes focus on
empowering marginalised groups and creating long-term societal impact. We
actively collaborate with NGOs, government bodies, and community
organisations to ensure our interventions are effective, inclusive, and aligned
with local needs.
6.3. Ethical Governance and Oversight
Saatvik is committed to strong corporate governance practices, ensuring
transparency, accountability, and ethical conduct in all aspects of business
operations. Our governance framework is designed to protect stakeholder
interests, strengthen business resilience, and support sustainable growth.
• Risk Managemen t: We have established a comprehensive enterprise risk
management framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across
strategic, operational, financial, and compliance areas. Risk assessments,
audits, and continuous monitoring enable proactive mitigation and ensure
business continuity.
• Board Oversight : Our Board of Directors provides strategic guidance,
oversight, and accountability for the company’s operations and sustainability
initiatives. The Board regularly reviews governance practices, operational
performance, ESG progress, and strategic priorities to align business
objectives with long-term stakeholder value creation .
• Transparent and Ethical Practices : Saatvik conducts its business with
integrity, transparency, and adherence to all applicable laws and regulations.
Ethical practices are embedded in our operations through robust policies on
anti-corruption, whistleblower mechanisms, and responsible busines s
conduct. We maintain open communication with stakeholders, ensuring
honesty, fairness, and accountability in all dealings.
• Training & Awareness on Ethical Practices: Saatvik ensures that all
employees, officers, and contractors are well -versed in ethical standards,

9
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
corporate governance principles, and compliance requirements. Regular
training programmes, workshops, and awareness sessions are conducted to
promote integrity, accountability, and responsible decision-making across all
levels of the organi sation. These program mes, including workshops and
interactive sessions, are designed to embed integrity, accountability, and
responsible decision -making across the organisation. Our target is to ensure
100% of employees are trained in ethical practices and governance by FY
2026.
• Sustainable Supply Chain and Procurement Practices : Saatvik shall
ensure that its supply chain and procurement activities are conducted
responsibly, ethically, and sustainably. Saatvik shall engage suppliers who
adhere to ESG standards, including compliance with applicable laws, labo ur
rights, and human rights. Sustainable sourcing practices shall prioriti se local
procurement, responsible material selection, and minimi sing environmental
impact throughout the supply chain. Regular assessments, audits, and
supplier engagement program mes shall be conducted to monitor
compliance, identify risks, and drive continuous improvement. The Company
shall integrate sustainability criteria into procurement decisions and
collaborate with suppliers to promote transparency, ethical practices, and
circular economy principles. Saatvik aims to achieve 100% compliance of
critical suppliers with Saatvik’s ESG standards by FY 20 30.
6.4 Career Management & Training
Saatvik is committed to implementing structured career management and
training practices to support employee development across all stages of the
employment lifecycle, including recruitment, performance evaluation, training,
career mobility, and professional development.
The Company shall ensure that recruitment, promotion, and career progression
processes are conducted in a transparent, objective, and merit -based manner.
Performance evaluation mechanisms shall be implemented to provide regular
feedback, identify developme nt needs, and support employee growth and
succession planning.
Saatvik shall provide training and development opportunities to enhance
technical, functional, behavioural, leadership, and sustainability -related

10
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
competencies. Training needs shall be identified based on role requirements,
business priorities, regulatory obligations, and future skill requirements.
The Company commits to ensuring 100% employee coverage for at least one
structured training programme annually by FY 2027.
Training effectiveness and workforce capability requirements shall be reviewed
periodically to support continuous improvement and long -term employability.
7. Roles and Responsibilities
Saatvik recognises that successful ESG implementation requires accountability at every
level. Saatvik has established a formal ESG Governance Structure to oversee, manage,
and implement ESG initiatives across the Group. This structure applies to all Saatvik
entities and is reviewed annually or in response to significant regulatory changes . The
following roles and responsibilities are defined in the Governance Structure to ensure
effective execution of the ESG Policy:
• Board of Directors : The Board serves as the apex body for ESG governance. It
provides strategic oversight, approves ESG policies and targets, reviews
performance reports and disclosures, and ensures ESG integration into risk
management, corporate strategy, and decision -making.
• ESG Co uncil: The ESG Council, chaired by the CEO, meets quarterly to review
performance, assess progress against sustainability goals, and guide the
Corporate Sustainability Team. It acts as a bridge between the Board and
management, translating strategic directives in to actionable initiatives and
promoting a culture of sustainability across the Group.
• Corporate Sustainability Team : This team leads the development and
implementation of ESG policies, program mes, and key performance indicators.
It ensures compliance with national and international standards such as SEBI
BRSR, EcoVadis, CDP , GRI, and UN SDGs, conducts materiality assessments,
maintains ESG data systems, and prepares the annual Sustainability Repo rt.
• Implementing Team : Comprising representatives from key functions such as
EHS, HR, Procurement, and Operations, the Implementing Team executes ESG
projects within their areas of responsibility. It embeds ESG considerations into

11

routine processes, monitors performance, and reports outcomes to the
Corporate Sustainability Team for consolidation and review.
• Plant-level ESG Specialists and Coordinators : These specialists oversee ESG
implementation at manufacturing and project sites. They coordinate cross -
departmental activities, collect and validate ESG data, ensure compliance with
EHS regulations, and support both internal and external audits and certifications.
• ESG Single Points of Contact (SPOCs): SPOCs act as departmental ESG
ambassadors across corporate and plant functions. They facilitate
implementation of ESG policies, provide data inputs for sustainability reporting,
promote awareness, and share best practices and improvement opportunities
within their respective teams.
