title: Employee Engagement, Communication & Grievance Redressal Policy

pages.text:
Employee Engagement,
Communication &
Grievance Redressal
Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its
meeting held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until
amended or replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Policy Statement
Saatvik Group is deeply committed to fostering a fair, ethical, and transparent
work environment that respects every individual. This policy is designed to foster
an open, transparent, and inclusive work environment, where employees feel
heard, valued, and empowered to contribute their best.
The Employee Engagement, Communication & Grievance Redressal Policy
outlines the framework for effective communication, proactive engagement, and
timely resolution of concerns or grievances. It ensures that all employees have
access to fair, consistent, an d confidential channels to raise issues, share
feedback, and contribute to initiatives that enhance workplace culture and
collaboration. To uphold this core value, we have established a formal grievance
management process that provides all employees and wo rkers with a structured
and confidential platform to voice and resolve their concerns in a time-bound and
impartial manner. This policy aims to address and resolve any dissatisfaction or
perceived injustice related to work conditions, interpersonal relationships, or the
application of company policies .
The policy also reinforces Saatvik’s stance on non -discrimination, equal
opportunity, freedom of association, and respect for human rights across its
workforce, including contractual, wherever applicable.
Our unwavering commitment is to ensure the identity of any employee raising a
genuine grievance is kept confidential, and that they are fully protected from any
negative repercussions or retaliation. The process is accessible, inclusive, and
designed to accommodate diverse reporting channels, ensuring that all
employees, regardless of literacy levels, location, or employment type, can raise
their concerns effectively. Conversely, any grievance found to be deliberately
untrue, frivolous, or malicious followi ng a thorough investigation will be subject
to appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with company policy. This
ensures the integrity of the process for everyone.
Furthermore, aggregate grievance data and trends will be reviewed periodically
by the Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) to drive systemic improvements.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
2. Policy Objectives
This policy aims to:
2.1. Foster a culture of open communication and mutual respect.
2.2. Strengthen employee engagement through structured feedback and
participation mechanisms.
2.3. Provide a transparent and accessible grievance redressal system.
2.4. Ensure timely resolution of concerns while maintaining confidentiality and
fairness.
2.5. Our primary objective is to offer a simple & accessible grievance redressal
mechanism, ensuring that all employees can raise issues without fear of
reprisal. This Grievance Management System, referred to as "VOICE UP , "
is designed with several key objectiv es in mind:
• Provide an Objective System: To establish a neutral and impartial
channel for raising complaints, ensuring that all grievances are reviewed
on their merits and without bias or favoritism.
• Support Formal Procedure: To provide a formal, documented process
that guides employees through a clear path for resolution, guaranteeing
that their concerns are taken seriously and not dismissed.
• Confidence and Transparency: To build trust among our employees by
demonstrating that their concerns will be handled with utmost care,
transparency, and confidentiality.
• Identify Systemic Gaps: To act as a diagnostic tool for management,
helping to identify and address any underlying issues, systemic failures,
or policy gaps that may be causing employee dissatisfaction.
• Prevent Escalation: To resolve minor disagreements and issues at the
earliest possible stage, preventing them from escalating into major
disputes that could negatively impact team morale and productivity.
• Alignment with ESG & SDGs : To contribute towards Saatvik’s broader
ESG commitments in line with promoting Employee Well -being,
upholding Human Rights and promoting UN Sustainable Development
Goals in general.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
3. Scope and Applicability
This policy titled, “Employee Engagement, Communication & Grievance
Redressal Policy” (“Policy”), is applicable across operations of Saatvik Green
Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group”
or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all on -roll/regular employees (including directors, officers,
permanent staff, trainees, probationers, and temporary workers) of the Saatvik
Group of Companies, regardless of their position, tenure, or business unit. For
contractual workers, we have laid out separate mechanism mentioned in Clause
12 – Grievance Handling for Contractual Workers.
4. Policy Commitments
Saatvik is committed to:
4.1. Encourage two -way communication through regular conversations with
Human Resource team, town halls, feedback surveys, and team huddles.
Town halls and feedback sessions shall be conducted at least once per
quarter to ensure employees are informed, engaged, and able to share
their perspectives.
4.2. Promote participative decision -making and idea-sharing platforms.
4.3. Recognise and celebrate employee contributions regularly.
4.4. Provide a safe, non -retaliatory environment for employees to voice
concerns.
4.5. Ensure grievances are addressed promptly, fairly, and confidentially.
Saatvik aims to resolve 90% of grievances within 14 working days, from the
date of receipt, in accordance with established protocols.
4.6. Maintain a structured escalation matrix for unresolved issues. All
employees shall undergo annual training on communication and
grievance redressal protocols to ensure awareness, understanding, and
compliance with the policy.
4.7. Uphold the highest standards of integrity, fairness, and respect.
4.8. Ensure all employees are aware of their rights and responsibilities.
4.9. Align grievance handling with Saatvik’s Code of Conduct.

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
5. Employee Engagement
Saatvik is committed to fostering employee alignment with the Company’s
mission of advancing sustainable energy solutions. The Company shall
implement structured engagement initiatives to encourage active participation,
collaboration, and contribution towa rds organisational goals, ensuring that
employees are informed, motivated, and empowered in their roles.
5.1. Purpose-Driven Culture: Saatvik shall foster a purpose -driven culture by
connecting employees to the Company’s sustainability goals through
internal campaigns, leadership communications, and project showcases.
5.2. Transparent Communication Channels: Saatvik shall maintain
transparent communication channels, including town halls, newsletters,
and team meetings, to ensure that employees are informed, engaged, and
able to participate meaningfully in organi sational discussions and
decision-making processes.
5.3. Recognition and Rewards: Saatvik shall operate a structured recognition
programme, conducted quarterly, to celebrate and reward employees’
achievements in areas such as innovation, collaboration, and
sustainability impact. Employees may be nominated by peers or
departments, and awards will be granted based on defined criteria.
5.4. Learning and Development: Saatvik shall promote continuous learning
and professional development through workshops, certifications,
mentorship programmes, and other learning initiatives. Programmes shall
be aligned with industry best practices, emerging trends, and
organisational needs to enhance employee skills and capabilities.
5.5. Feedback Mechanisms: Saatvik shall maintain structured feedback
mechanisms, including annual engagement surveys, periodic pulse
surveys, and anonymous suggestion channels, to systematically capture
employee sentiment. Insights from these mechanisms shall be analy sed
and used to inform decision -making, enhance workplace practices, and
drive continuous improvement.
5.6. Inclusive Work Environment: Saatvik is committed to fostering a diverse,
equitable, and inclusive workplace. Policies and practices shall be

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
implemented to ensure that all employees are treated with respect, that
every voice is heard, and that opportunities for participation and
contribution are accessible to all.
6. Scope of Grievance Redressal
The "VOICE UP" system is tailored to address grievances in the following key
areas. Any other grievance that does not fit neatly into these categories will be
classified as "miscellaneous" and handled accordingly to ensure no concern
goes unaddressed. This ensures that every stakeholder’s concern is recogni sed
and processed in a fair and transparent manner, in alignment with Saatvik’s ESG
commitments.
Grievance Type Key Grievance Area
Errors in Salary
Payment
Non-communicated deductions, mistakes in wage calculations, or
discrepancies in overtime payments (only if previously raised with HR and
unresolved after a reasonable period).
Supervision
Misbehaviour, unfair treatment, unprofessional conduct, lack of guidance,
or work harassment by a direct manager or a senior leader. This will be
handled with strict anonymity and protection from retaliation.
General Working
Conditions
Concerns related to the working environment, issues with safety and
sanitation, hazardous working conditions, unfair leave and attendance
management, and interpersonal relationships within the department. This
includes aspects of occupational health and safety and workplace well-
being.
Process &
Policies
Concerns regarding the consistent and fair non-implementation of
applicable company policies.
Welfare
Measures
Issues concerning the quality or availability of company-provided facilities,
such as transportation, canteen services, and township management (if
available) where these facilities are a part of the employment offering. This
reflects Saatvik’s responsibility to ensure equitable and safe access to
basic employee welfare infrastructure.
Miscellaneous
Any grievance that does not fit within the above categories will be reviewed
under a “miscellaneous” classification to ensure no concern is overlooked.
This flexible approach ensures inclusivity and responsiveness.
It is important to note that this system is not a substitute for existing policies and does not cover matters related to
performance appraisals, merit increments, promotions, medical insurance, disciplinary actions, whistle-blower cases, or
sexual harassme nt, as separate, speciali sed processes and committees are in place to address these issues with the

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
appropriate legal and professional oversight. In addition, grievances related to violations of human rights, labor rights, or
ethical practices within Saatvik’s operations may also be raised under this system.
7. Grievance Redressal Exceptions
In rare cases where grievance is raised against a member of the Grievance
Redressal Committee (GRC), an exception to the standard process is permitted
to ensure fairness and impartiality. The employee can bypass the normal
procedure and directly email the Location HR. Location HR will take on the role
of the primary investigator, ensuring the matter is handled by a neutral party. The
timeline for resolution remains 14 working days, and the decision of the Location
HR is final and binding for the grievance.
If the grievance is against the Location HR themselves, the matter will be
escalated directly to the Group CHRO, whose decision will be considered final.
This structured bypass mechanism is in place to eliminate any potential conflict
of interest.
In addition, grievances falling under critical categories such as hazardous
working conditions, human rights violations, or labor rights abuses will be given
priority handling under this exception mechanism, with immediate interim
measures taken to safegua rd the complainant’s safety and well -being while the
investigation proceeds.
8. Roles & Responsibilities of Grievance Redressal
Committee GRC & Key Stakeholders
The grievance redressal process is a collaborative effort involving several key
stakeholders, each with a defined role to ensure a smooth and fair resolution.
8.1. Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC): The Grievance Redressal
Committee (GRC) at Saatvik Group is the central authority for all employee
grievance matters. The committee's role is to ensure a fair, unbiased, and
transparent process for resolving employee co ncerns. This includes
assessing all issues raised by employees, assigning a dedicated
investigating officer for a thorough review, and making well -informed
decisions based on the facts and evidence presented. The GRC also
collaborates with other stakeholde rs and appellate authorities to ensure
grievances are resolved within the specified timelines and to the best

8
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
possible extent.
The GRC's responsibilities are clearly defined to ensure a systematic
approach to grievance resolution. The committee, led by a chairperson
(nominated annually by GRC members), oversees the day-to-day operations
and coordinates with GRC secretary and all members.
• Acknowledgement: Acknowledge every grievance promptly.
• Investigation: Oversee a comprehensive investigation conducted by the
appointed officer. For grievances involving hazardous working
conditions or potential human rights violations, the GRC will ensure
immediate interim measures are implemented to safeguard employees.
• Documentation: Ensure the investigating officer documents the case
and provides a report to aid the GRC in its decision-making.
• Timeline: Adhere to a strict 14-working-day timeline for resolution.
• Record Keeping: Maintain detailed records of all grievances and their
respective investigations. Aggregate data will be reviewed quarterly for
systemic improvements.
• Guidance: Guide stakeholders in finding and validating effective
solutions.
8.2. GRC Secretary: This role is central to the entire process. The GRC
Secretary is the primary point of contact, responsible for acknowledging
the grievance, conducting a preliminary fact -finding investigation and/or
assigning neutral investigator, tracking the progress of the case, tabling the
result of the investigation and its outcomes/decision before the GRC,
closure of the grievance (need to take consensus of the GRC members),
and officially communicating the final decision to the employee. They are
the custodian of gr ievance records and the primary system administrator
ensuring compliance, confidentiality, and timelines.
8.3. GRC Members: The committee members are responsible for objectively
assessing the details of the grievance, and making a final, appropriate
decision based on the evidence and facts presented during the
investigation.

9
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8.4. HR Team: This team is specifically responsible for providing assistance to
investigations and providing technical solutions for grievances related to
salary payment errors or discrepancies. They also support awareness
campaigns to ensure employees and contractual workers know how to
access the grievance system.
8.5. Reporting Manager: In cases related to Learning & Development and
General Working Conditions, the reporting manager is expected to provide
all necessary support and information to the investigator while
maintaining absolute confidentiality to ensure the integrity of the proc ess.
They are also responsible for promptly addressing grievances within their
control to prevent escalation.
8.6. Location HR : The Location HR is responsible for investigating and
resolving grievances specifically related to the implementation and
interpretation of company policies and processes - Non implementation
of applicable policy.
8.7. Appellate Authority: The Appellate Authority is the final recourse for
employees whose grievances were not resolved to their satisfaction by the
Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC). In most cases, the CEO acts as
the Appellate Authority. Their decision is final and binding on all parties
involved.
8.8. Appellate Process and Responsibilities:
• An employee has 30 days from the GRC's decision to appeal. The
process is as follows:
• Employee's Action: The employee sends an email to the Head HR
explaining their dissatisfaction with the GRC's outcome.
• HR-Head's Role: The Location HR conducts a preliminary review with the
GRC Secretary and the GRC. The findings are then shared with the CEO
(Appellate Authority).
• Appellate Authority's Role: The Appellate Authority reviews the case,
which may involve consulting with the GRC and the original investigating
officer. They have the option to launch a new investigation if they deem
necessary.
• Decision and Communication: The Appellate Authority's decision is
conveyed to the employee by Location HR, first via a call or face-to-face

Policy Date: 11th December 2025
meeting, followed by a formal email. This final decision is to be made
within 14 working days of receiving the appeal.
9. The "VOICE UP" Operating Principles
Our grievance process is governed by a set of clear operating principles designed
to ensure efficiency, fairness, and transparency and alignment with Saatvik’s ESG
commitments:
9.1. Timeliness: Grievance resolution, from the moment of receipt to its final
closure, must be completed within 14 working days. This strict timeline is
a key pillar of our commitment to efficiency. Grievances involving
hazardous working conditions, health and safety, or human rights
violations will receive priority attention with immediate interim safeguards
implemented while the investigation proceeds.
9.2. Acknowledgement: The GRC Secretary must formally acknowledge the
receipt of the grievance within 3 working days of it being emailed. This
provides the employee with a clear timeline for the next steps.
Acknowledgement will include a unique tracking number and assurance
of confidentiality and protection from retaliation.
9.3. Collective Decision: Final decisions on grievances are made basis the
majority views of the GRC i.e. with at least half of the members agreeing to
the decision, ensuring that the resolution is not based on a single
individual's opinion.
9.4. Expedited Investigation: The GRC Secretary's preliminary investigation is
a critical step to gather initial facts and information, which helps to
streamline the formal investigation process and reach a resolution faster.
Where systemic gaps are identified, recommendations will also be
submitted for policy or process improvements.
9.5. Appeal Process: Appeals to the Appellate Authority must be submitted
within 30 days of receiving the GRC's decision, allowing employees ample
time to consider their options.
9.6. Prompt Appeal Response: The Appellate Authority must respond to an
appeal within 14 working days to ensure the grievance is not prolonged
unnecessarily.

11
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
9.7. Conflict of Interest Protocol: Grievances raised against GRC members
are handled by the Location HR within 14 working days to avoid any
conflict of interest, and their decision is final in these specific cases. If the
grievance involves the Location HR, it will escalate to the CHRO, and if it
involves both, it will escalate directly to the Appellate Authority (CEO).
9.8. Accessibility & Inclusivity: The “VOICE UP” system will ensure multiple
reporting channels (email, helpline, drop -boxes, in-person reporting) and
local language support, so that all employees, including contractual, can
raise concerns without barriers.
10. Grievance Redressal Process and Timelines
Our online grievance management system is configured to provide a simple,
easy-to-use, and intuitive experience. In addition to email, grievances may also
be raised through multiple channels such as calling with Location HR , physical
drop-boxes at plant and office locations, or in -person reporting to HR
representatives, ensuring accessibility for all employees and those with limited
digital access. The process is as follows:
10.1. Raise a Grievance: The employee initiates the process by sending an
email to grievance_internal@saatvikgroup.com. The email should clearly
mention a concise title of the grievance, the severity level of the issue (e.g.,
low, medium, high), and a detailed description of the incident covering all
relevant facts such as date, time, location, and people involved. Employees
are encouraged to attach any supporting documents or evidence (emails,
photos, screenshots, written notes, etc.) that can help provide a clearer
context and assist in resolving the grievance effectively.
10.2. Acknowledgement: Upon submission, the GRC Secretary is
automatically notified. Within three working days, the Secretary will
formally acknowledge the grievance on the email, providing a unique
reference number for tracking purposes and confirming that the process
has begun.
10.3. Preliminary Investigation & Assignment: The GRC Secretary reviews the
case to ensure all necessary information is provided. They then table the
grievance before the GRC Committee, who collectively review the details
and may appoint a neutral investigator based on the grievance category.

12

Policy Date: 11th December 2025
10.4. Investigation: The GRC Secretary and/or appointed investigator conducts
a thorough and confidential investigation. This may involve interviewing
the aggrieved employee, the accused party, and any relevant witnesses,
as well as reviewing documents and other evidence. The investigation
must be carried out in a manner that ensures fairness, avoids conflicts of
interest, and respects the dignity of all parties involved. The investigator
compiles a detailed report of their findings.
10.5. Resolution: The investigator reports back their findings to the GRC
Secretary (In case of assigning an investigator). The GRC Secretary then
presents these findings to the full GRC Committee, which meets to
discuss the facts and arrive at a final, binding decision reg arding the
resolution of the grievance. Final decisions on grievances are made basis
the majority views of the GRC i.e. with at least half of the members
agreeing to the decision.
10.6. Closure: The GRC Secretary communicates the final decision and the
details of the resolution to the employee via the email or physical letter .
Where relevant, employees will also be informed of their right to appeal to
the Appellate Authority. Once the resolution is delivered, the GRC
Secretary officially closes the grievance, marking the successful
completion of the entire process.
10.7. The entire process, from raising the grievance to its final closure, is
designed to be completed within a maximum of 14 working days. The
ultimate responsibility for ensuring a timely closure lies with the GRC
Secretary and the GRC, who are tasked with uph olding the principles of
this policy.
11. Handling of Records & Data
All grievances will be documented and maintained in a standardi sed format to
ensure consistency, transparency, and traceability. Each grievance will be
assigned a unique reference number, and a record will be maintained (refer
Annexure A).
11.1. Type of Grievance may include issues such as Errors in Salary Payment,
Supervision, General Working Conditions, Process & Policies, and Welfare
Measures.

13
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
11.2. Evidence must be collected and maintained in both digital and hard copy
formats, including emails, documents, photographs, meeting notes, and
interview transcripts recorded during the investigation process.
11.3. Records will be updated at every stage of the grievance lifecycle
(submission, review, investigation, resolution, and closure).
11.4. All records must be stored securely to maintain confidentiality while
ensuring accessibility for authori sed personnel.
12. Grievance Handling for Contractual Workers
12.1. A grievance redressal process has been laid out for contractual workers to
ensure that their concerns are heard, addressed, and resolved in a timely
and impartial manner. The aim is to provide them with a clear channel of
communication and a step -by-step escalation path, so that issues such
as workplace conditions, supervision, welfare measures, or other matters
are dealt with fairly, without unnecessary delays or complications :
• Step 1: The worker will raise the grievance by sending an email to
the Line Manager with a copy to the Principal Employer and Plant
HR or they may intimate over phone , through drop -box or verbal
communication.
• Step 2: The Line Manager will initiate the investigation, review the
facts, and share the findings and decision with the deputed
worker with a copy to Plant HR and Plant Head.
• Step 3: If the worker is not satisfied with the resolution, the
matter may be further escalated to the Plant HR for review.
• Step 4: If still unresolved, the grievance will be finally escalated
to the Plant Head
12.2. Special Cases:
• Special Case 1: If the grievance is against the Line Manager, the
matter will be taken directly to the Plant Head, whose decision
shall be considered final.
• Special Case 2: If the grievance is against the Plant HR or Plant
Head, the matter will be escalated to the CHRO, whose decision
shall be considered final.

14
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Special Case 3: If the grievance relates to hazardous working
conditions, potential human rights violations, or serious safety
concerns, interim protective measures must be immediately
implemented (such as temporary reassignment or suspension of
unsafe activities) until the matter is resolved. These cases will be
given priority and escalated to the Plant Head/CHRO as required.
12.3. Confidentiality & Protection:
All grievances raised by contractual workers will be handled with strict
confidentiality, and workers will be protected from retaliation or adverse
action for raising genuine concerns. Anonymous grievances will also be
accepted if sufficient details are pr ovided to initiate an investigation.
12.4. Monitoring & Reporting:
All grievances raised by contractual workers will be recorded, tracked,
and reviewed quarterly by Plant HR and the GRC.
13. Continual Improvement
Continual improvement under Saatvik’s Integrated Management System shall be
achieved through internal and external audits, management reviews, proactive
monitoring of unsafe acts and conditions, and active worker participation.
Findings from incident inves tigations, risk assessments, and audit outcomes
shall be reviewed by management and the Safety Committees to enhance the
effectiveness of occupational health and safety practices and ensure alignment
with emerging national and international regulations.
14. Worker Participation and Consultation
A formal Employee Well Being Committee shall be established at each plant,
comprising representatives from management, supervisors, and workers,
including contractual staff. This Committee shall meet periodically and as
required following significant incid ents to review employee wellbeing and
grievances redressal performance, identify problems, and recommend
corrective measures.

Proceedings of all meetings shall be recorded, communicated to relevant
personnel, and monitored for timely implementation. Saatvik shall protect all
committee members and participants from any form of reprisal and shall ensure
that all suggestions or conc erns raised by workers are acknowledged, reviewed,
and acted upon wherever feasible. Regular consultations ensure that decisions
reflect the collective voice of the workforce, promoting transparency, trust, and
shared ownership of organi sational goals.
15. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices,
stakeholder expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this
Policy shall be made i n writing and will become effective upon approval by ESG
Council of Saatvik.

1. Prologue
Saatvik Group’s commitment to equal opportunity promotes an inclusive work
environment that values and accepts the diverse cultural and social backgrounds of its
staff.
2. Objective
Saatvik is committed to creating a secure and inclusive work environment where all its
stakeholders, such as Employees, Agents, Vendors, and Partners, can work and pursue
business in an atmosphere free from any sexual harassment, exploitation, and
intimidation.
Saatvik values every employee working with them and is committed to protecting their
dignity and self -respect. Further, Saatvik is determined to maintain personal dignity;
promote a working environment where both genders complement each other as equals,
and to strive for maximum productivity.
The objective of this Policy is to ensure equality of opportunity for all employees, free
from discrimination on any grounds, including race, religion, belief, sex, colour, creed,
age, national or ethnic origin, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, political
affiliation, or physical ability. This commitment reinforces Saatvik’s dedication to
fostering a culture that values diversity, equity, and respect for all.
3. Scope & Applicability
This Policy shall be referred to as “Equal Employment Opportunity Policy” (“Policy”) and
shall be applicable to all the employees of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its
subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
4. Policy, Procedures & Guidelines
4.1 The objective of this policy is to provide employment equality to all, irrespective of
gender, marital or civil partnership status, parental status, pregnancy, religion or
belief, political opinion, caste, race (including colour, nationality, ethnic or national
origin), disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, union
membership, or any other protected characteristic under law.
4.2 Saatvik is opposed to all forms of unlawful and unfair discrimination. All job
applicants, employees, and others who work for Saatvik will be treated fairly and

3

will not be discriminated against on any of the above grounds. Saatvik respects
everyone and values the diversity of backgrounds. This Policy is to be practiced
upholding values of fairness and respect for humanity, recognizing the unique
strengths, compet encies, and talents of individuals. The decisions about
recruitment and selection, promotion, training, or any other benefit will be made
objectively and without unlawful discrimination.
4.3 This Policy will operate in conjunction with Recruitment & Selection, Performance
Management — Performance Analysis, Learning & Development, Induction,
Probation & Confirmation, Whistleblowing Policy, Grievance & Disputes
Procedure, Leave & Holidays, Trans fer, Medical Insurance, Canteen, Transport,
Safety & Security.
4.4 This includes provisions for assistive devices, barrier -free accessibility, and other
provisions for persons with disabilities, including travel, loans & advances,
reasonable working hours, infrastructure facilities and amenities, inclusive of
special provisions for transgender persons & persons with disabilities.
4.5 The confidentiality of employees’ gender identity shall be respected at all times. In
compliance with the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, Saatvik
will appoint a Complaint Officer. The company will also identify posts suitable for
persons with disabilities and appoint a Liaison Officer to oversee the recruitment
and inclusion of persons with disabilities.
4.6 Saatvik is committed to promoting equality of opportunity for all persons,
promoting a good and harmonious working environment in which all persons are
treated with respect, and preventing occurrences of unlawful direct
discrimination, indirect discriminat ion, harassment, and victimization.
4.7 The company will also ensure that persons with disabilities are given preference in
matters such as transfer, posting, training, and other terms of employment.
4.8 Saatvik will take lawful affirmative or positive action where appropriate. Any breach
of this Policy will be treated as misconduct and may result in disciplinary
proceedings.
5. Responsibilities
5.1 The Head of Human Resources is responsible for implementing this Policy,
coordinating the application / implementation of this Policy, and monitoring its
effectiveness.

5.2 Reporting Heads are responsible for ensuring that this Policy is implemented
within their departments, offices, projects, and teams. All employees have a
personal responsibility to treat other employees fairly, value and respect others,
and ensure that no one is harassed, victimized or bullied in the workplace.
5.3 We expect all Saatvik employees to abide by this Policy and contribute to
fostering an equitable and inclusive work environment, which is the core
objective of this policy.
6. Training & Awareness
Saatvik will provide regular training and awareness programs on equal employment
opportunity, non-discrimination, and unconscious bias. Training will include specialized
sessions for managers, HR personnel, and recruitment staff. The company will also
extend awareness sessions to contractors and other stakeholders, where relevant, to
strengthen diversity, equity, and inclusion across the value chain.
7. Grievance Redressal
7.1 If any employee or applicant believes they have been subjected to discrimination
or unfair treatment in employment, they are encouraged to report the matter
promptly using the channel given in Internal Grievance Redress Mechanism.
Complaints will be invest igated promptly, fairly, and confidentially, with
protection against retaliation.
7.2 The Saatvik Human Resource Head is responsible for hearing such claims,
investigating the issue, and determining appropriate action punishment as per
Saatvik’s Policy or as per the provision of Saatvik's whistleblower mechanism.
7.3 Upon receiving any complaint, Saatvik Human Resource Head will conduct
interviews, gather all relevant information(s) and investigate all claims discreetly.
7.4 Saatvik will never disclose who made a complaint to anyone or give out
information that may help others identify that person.
7.5 Punishment for discriminatory behaviour depends on the severity of the offence.
Employees who harass their colleagues will go through our disciplinary process,
and we may reprimand, demote or terminate them depending on the severity of
their offence.
7.6 Saatvik encourages all employees to remain aware of implicit biases and to report
any instance of discrimination experienced or observed in the workplace.

promote fairness, equality, and inclusion within the workplace.

Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board.

1. Prologue
The Saatvik Group of Companies (“Saatvik”) is committed to conducting all business
operations with integrity, transparency, and accountability. Fraud, defined as any
deliberate act of deception intended to secure unlawful or unfair gain, is strictly
prohibited. Saatvik adopts a zero -tolerance approach to fraud and related misconduct
and strives to maintain a workplace culture that promotes honesty and ethical
behaviour across all operations.
2. Objective
This Policy aims to:
2.1. Establish a structured framework for preventing, detecting, and responding to
fraudulent activities.
2.2. Promote transparency and ethical conduct through effective internal controls,
awareness, and oversight.
2.3. Ensure that all employees and partners understand their role in maintaining
Saatvik’s zero-tolerance stance on fraud.
3. Scope of the Policy
This Policy, titled “ Fraud Risk Control ” (“Policy”), is applicable across operations of
Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik
Group” or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff,
trainees, probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers,
agents, business partners, and any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or
indirectly.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4. Policy Commitments
Saatvik shall:
4.1. Act in full transparency and condemn any illegal or deceptive act to gain
advantage.
4.2. Implement robust fraud detection and reporting mechanisms.
4.3. Investigate all reported or suspected cases of fraud promptly and fairly.
4.4. Take corrective, disciplinary, and legal actions as warranted.
4.5. Continuously monitor and improve internal controls to prevent recurrence.
5. Quantitative Commitments
5.1. Train 100 % of employees on fraud awareness and prevention annually by FY
2027.
5.2. Undertake annual third -party audits to review compliance with fraud -control
procedures by FY 2028.
6. Training and Awareness
Saatvik shall organi se regular training and awareness progra mmes to help employees
recognise fraud indicators and reporting procedures. Sessions will be held at least once
every year as part of the company’s ongoing ethics education.
7. Fraud Risk Identification and Controls
Saatvik shall conduct periodic fraud risk assessments to identify areas vulnerable to
fraudulent practices. The Internal Audit team shall evaluate existing controls,
segregation of duties, and approval hierarchies. Findings from these reviews will inform
improvements in control design and monitoring frequency.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8. Reporting and Grievance Mechanism
Concerns or suspicions of fraud may be raised to the Audit Committee via CFO of
Saatvik by writing email at abani.jha@saatvikgroup.com;
All complaints will be acknowledged within 7 working days and investigated within 30
working days, or longer if complexity demands.
9. Roles and Responsibilities
The Board of Directors shall provide overall oversight and approve necessary updates to
this Policy, while the Audit Committee shall monitor its implementation and review the
effectiveness of internal controls and investigations. Department Heads shall ens ure
that preventive controls are embedded in their daily operations. All employees and
contractors are expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity, remain vigilant to
potential fraud risks, and immediately report any suspected or actual fraudulent activity
through authorised reporting channels .
10. Disciplinary Action
Individuals proven to have engaged in or facilitated fraud shall face disciplinary
measures up to and including termination of employment or contract, restitution of
losses, and/or legal proceedings, depending on severity.
11. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder
expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made i n
writing and will become effective upon approval by a resolution of the Board of Directors
of Saatvik.
Disclaimer: This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. CFO Office of Saatvik is the final authority in
interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy. Saatvik reserves the right to modify t he
Policy from time to time.

title: Grievance Redressal Policy for External Stakeholders

pages.text:
Grievance Redressal
Policy
for External Stakeholders
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Policy Statement
Saatvik Group is committed to conducting business ethically, transparently,
sustainably, and responsibly. We recognize that our operations and supply chain
may have impacts , real or perceived , on external stakeholders (vendors, sub -
vendors, service providers, customers, affected communities, etc.).
We are committed to providing accessible, fair, and transparent mechanisms for all
external stakeholders to raise grievances, request redress or remediation, and
ensure that these are addressed promptly, impartially, and without retaliation.
This External Grievance Redressal Policy (the “Policy”) aims to fulfill Saatvik’s
accountability obligations under ESG, human rights, and stakeholder engagement
standards and aligns with recognized good practice for operational -level grievance
mechanisms and applicable sustainability reporting expectations .
The mechanism is supplementary to, and not a substitute for, judicial or regulatory
remedies where stakeholders choose those routes.
Saatvik is committed to delivering high-quality, reliable, and safe solar products and
services while ensuring that stakeholder feedback, queries, and grievances are
handled with transparency, fairness, and continuous improvement in mind.
2. Objectives
The objectives of this Policy are to:
2.1. Provide a clear, accessible and trusted channel for external stakeholders
(vendors, sub -vendors, communities, suppliers, customers, other third
parties) to raise concerns, complaints or grievances related to our operations,
policies, contractual performance, or any adverse social / environmental
impacts. This includes issues connected to human rights, labor rights, ethics,
supply-chain practices, products safety and alignment with our ESG
commitments.
2.2. Ensure grievances are assessed, investigated, and resolved in a timely,
impartial, and transparent manner.
2.3. Prevent recurrence by identifying root causes, systemic risks, and learning
from grievances.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
2.4. Build stakeholder trust, strengthen relationships and improve our operational
and ESG performance.
2.5. Assure that use of this mechanism does not impede access to legal or
regulatory recourse and provide an option to escalate unresolved cases to
independent forums or oversight bodies where appropriate.
2.6. Address customer grievances and feedback effectively to strengthen product
stewardship, improve service quality, and enhance customer satisfaction.
3. Scope and Applicability
This Policy, titled “Grievance Redressal Policy for External Stakeholders”, is applicable
across operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively
referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
3.1. This Policy applies to grievances raised by external stakeholders including:
• Vendors, suppliers, contractors, sub-vendors
• Local communities, affected persons
• NGOs, civil society organizations, other third parties
• Service providers, consultants, business partners
• Customers
3.2. Types of grievances may include, but are not limited to:
• Contractual performance disputes, delays or non -fulfilment
• Product quality or performance issues
• Delays in delivery or response
• Payment issues, pricing, non -compliance with terms
• Environmental or social issues (pollution, disturbance, safety, worker
welfare)
• Human rights or labor rights concerns in supply chain
• Discrimination, harassment, or unfair treatment by our agents / third
parties
• Breach of laws, ethics, codes of conduct

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Health or safety risks associated with the use of solar modules or
systems
• Misrepresentation or inadequate information regarding products or
services
• Any adverse impact or risk perceived to arise from our operations
• ESG-related concerns (e.g., carbon footprint, climate risk, biodiversity
impact, supply chain transparency, product stewardship, data privacy &
security)
• Concerns related to conflict mineral issues including mineral extraction,
trade, handling and export in conflict -affected areas.
3.3. Exceptions / Exclusions
• Internal employee grievances (these should be addressed under the
internal HR grievance mechanism)
• Grievances already resolved via a different legal or arbitration process,
unless specifically submitted here
• Frivolous, malicious or duplicate grievances (after due screening)
• Grievances outside our jurisdictional/regional footprint or beyond the
scope of our influence
• Grievances that lack sufficient detail for investigation
It is important to note that this system is not a substitute for existing legal processes or commercial
contracts that contain their own dispute resolution clauses. This policy does not cover matters
already under litigation or arbitration. In addition, gr ievances related to violations of human rights,
labor rights, or ethical practices within Saatvik’s operations and supply chain may also be raised
under this system.
4. Basic Principles and Governance
This Policy has been developed in accordance with the following guiding
frameworks, principles, and governance standards that underpin Saatvik’s
approach to ethical and responsible business conduct:
4.1. Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR)

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4.2. IFC Performance Standards (particularly PS1 on Assessment and
Management of Environmental and Social Risks and Impacts),
4.3. UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs),
4.4. ISO 26000 Guidance on Social Responsibility.
5. Guiding Principles
The grievance mechanism shall adhere to the following principles :
5.1. Accessibility: Multiple channels for lodging grievances (written, email,
phone, in-person, web portal) in relevant local languages; low to no cost to
complainants.
5.2. Legitimacy / Impartiality: The process should be seen as fair and
independent, minimizing bias or conflicts of interest.
5.3. Transparency & Predictability: Clear procedures, timelines,
communications, status updates.
5.4. Confidentiality & Anonymity: Stakeholders can lodge grievances
anonymously or request confidentiality; their identity and information is
protected.
5.5. Non-retaliation: No person raising grievance shall suffer retaliation,
retribution or discrimination for doing so. This commitment applies equally to
suppliers’ and contractors’ workers.
5.6. Equitable & Proportionate: Remedies should be in proportion to
harm/impact, and fair to parties.
5.7. Dialogue & Participation: Engage the complainant in dialogue, hearing their
side, offering opportunity to be heard or accompanied.
5.8. Remedy & Closure: Provide appropriate remedies (apology, compensation,
corrective actions, changes in practices) and formally close grievances with
agreement and documentation.
5.9. Continuous Learning: Capture trends, root causes and systemic issues and
reflect learnings in policies and procedures.
5.10. Right to appeal: Not prevent complainants from using legal or regulatory
avenues if not satisfied with outcomes.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
6. Roles and Responsibility
Role Responsibility
Chief Finance Officer (CFO) & Chief
Human Resource Officer (CHRO)
Joint custodians of this Policy; oversight and
alignment with governance.
Heads of Departments (HODs)
For grievances related to their functional area (e.g.
operations, procurement, environment, legal), HODs
will be part of the investigation, resolution, and
follow-up process.
Grievance Redressal Committee
(GRC)
A cross-functional committee (see section 6) that
reviews serious/complex grievances, gives oversight,
ensures fairness and final decisions.
Grievance Officer / Secretariat
A designated person or team responsible for intake,
registration, tracking, coordination of investigations,
communication with complainants.
Investigation Team / Subject Matter
Experts
Experts from relevant departments (Procurement,
Legal, Sustainability, Operations) who examine and
propose resolution.
Internal Audit / Compliance / ESG
Oversight
Periodically review the grievance mechanism’s
functioning, audit sample cases, provide
recommendations.
All Employees, Vendors,
Contractors
Must cooperate with grievance investigations,
provide necessary information, support resolution.

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
7. Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC)
7.1. To enhance impartiality and oversight, a Grievance Redressal Committee
(GRC) is constituted:
• Chair: CFO or CHRO ( On rotation every year)
• Members: Heads of key functions (Procurement, Legal, Operations, ESG
/ Sustainability, Compliance, others)
• Secretary: Grievance Officer
7.2. Mandate of GRC:
• Review and approve (or reject) proposed resolution for significant,
sensitive or escalated grievances
• Ensure decisions are consistent, fair, and align with policy principles
• Monitor systemic trends, root -cause analyses, recommend policy
changes
• Oversee appeals and escalation
• Report (at periodic intervals) to executive leadership / board on
grievance performance, unresolved issues, lessons learned .
7.3. GRC shall have a clear quorum, decision -making rules, and timelines
defined. Quorum must include at least one independent member (internal
audit / ESG advisor) for decisions on human rights or ESG -related grievances.

8
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8. Grievance Redressal Mechanism / Process
8.1. Submission
• Stakeholder submits grievance via one or more channels (e.g. web
form, email, postal mail, phone, in -person at designated offices).
Official email id is grievance.ext@saatvikgroup.com where anyone can
submit their grievance.
• Provide minimum information: complainant name/contact (or indicate
anonymity), date, description of grievance, how/when it occurred,
parties involved, evidence, expectation / desired remedy
8.2. Registration & Acknowledgement
• Grievance Officer logs the grievance in a secure grievance registry
(assign unique reference number, date of receipt, categorization)
• Acknowledgment sent to complainant within a defined period including
reference number, expected timeline for response
8.3. Preliminary Screening / Eligibility Assessment
• Determine whether grievance is admissible (within scope, not frivolous,
not duplicative)
• If inadmissible, send explanation to complainant and close the case
(with documented reason)
• If admissible, classify the severity / priority (e.g. low / medium / high)
8.4. Investigation & Fact Finding
• Convene subject matter experts, collect relevant documents, interview
complainant, involved parties, witnesses
• If needed, site visits or third -party verification
• Maintain confidentiality, impartiality, opportunity for parties to present
their perspective
• For grievances relating to communities, investigations will follow
culturally appropriate engagement protocols (as per IFC PS1).

9
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8.5. Propose Resolution / Remedy
• Based on investigation, draft a proposed resolution (corrective actions,
compensation, process changes, apology, monitoring)
• For high or complex cases, escalate proposal to GRC for review and
approval
• Seek feedback from complainant on whether remedy is acceptable
8.6. Decision & Communication
• Final decision (accepted, partially accepted, or rejected) is documented
• Communicate the decision to complainant (within prescribed timeline)
along with reasoning, action plan, timeframes, and (if allowed) option to
appeal
• Implementation / Follow-up
• Ensure implementation of corrective actions, monitor the outcomes
• Maintain dialogue with complainant during implementation
• If the complainant is not satisfied, further review / escalation or appeal
may be initiated
8.7. Closure & Feedback
• Once agreed remedy is implemented and accepted, formally close the
grievance
• Seek feedback from complainant (satisfaction, process feedback)
through service calls
• Document closure and lessons learned
8.8. Monitoring, Reporting & Review
• Periodic reporting (quarterly, annually) on number, types, status and
outcomes of grievances
• Analysis of trends, root causes, systemic issues
• Internal audit / compliance review, and periodic review of the grievance
mechanism itself (to assess effectiveness)
• Update policy / procedures as needed

10
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8.9. Timeline
• Acknowledgement: within 5 –7 business days
• Eligibility determination: within 10 business days
• Investigation completed and proposed resolution: within 30 days
• Final decision and communication: within 45 days
• For complex cases, extension permissible with notification to
complainant (with reasons)
• These timeline benchmarks mirror good practice in project -level
grievance systems
9. Handling of Records & Data
All grievances will be documented and maintained in a standardized format to
ensure consistency, transparency, and traceability. Each grievance will be assigned
a unique reference number, and a record will be maintained (refer Annexure A).
9.1. Evidence must be collected and maintained in digital /hard copy formats,
including emails, documents, photographs, meeting notes, and interview
transcripts recorded during the investigation process.
9.2. Records will be updated at every stage of the grievance lifecycle (submission,
review, investigation, resolution, and closure).
9.3. All records must be stored securely to maintain confidentiality while ensuring
accessibility for authorized personnel.
10. Quantitative Commitments
10.1. Saatvik aims to achieve and maintain a complaint resolution rate of 100%
within the committed timelines and reduce repeat complaints by 5% annually
through corrective and preventive measures.
10.2. Ensure that 100% of external stakeholders are informed about the grievance
redressal mechanism by FY 2027 through contractual communication,
vendor onboarding, and customer touchpoints.

11
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
11. Review and Amendments:
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices,
stakeholder expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy
shall be made i n writing and will become effective upon approval of ESG Council of
Saatvik.
