Health and Safety Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness:
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
The Saatvik Group (“ Saatvik”) is committed to ensuring the safety, health, and well -
being of its employees and all individuals who may be affected by its operations.
Protecting people is fundamental to Saatvik’s values and to sustainable business
success.
We strive to embed a Zero Harm culture by integrating safety into every aspect of our
work, preventing injury and illness, and fostering shared responsibility across all levels
of the organisation.
2. Objective
This Policy aims to:
2.1 Protect people by preventing work -related injuries, illnesses, and unsafe acts
through proactive risk management.
2.2 Comply with all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements on Quality,
Environment, Health and Safety through the Integrated Management System
(IMS) aligned with ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018.
2.3 Foster wellbeing and a culture of care through leadership commitment and
employee engagement.
2.4 Pursue continual improvement in safety performance through monitoring and
evaluation.
3. Scope of the Policy
This Policy, titled “Health and Safety Policy” (“ Policy”), is applicable across operations
of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the
“Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff,
trainees, probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers,
agents, business partners, and any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or
indirectly.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4. Policy Commitments
Saatvik is committed to:
4.1 Embedding health and safety into every aspect of business operations, ensuring
it is integral to planning, execution, and decision -making.
4.2 Providing safe and healthy working environments by identifying hazards,
implementing controls, and supplying appropriate PPE.
4.3 Enhancing competence and participation through structured training,
communication, and feedback mechanisms.
4.4 Supporting holistic wellbeing via regular health check -ups and awareness
programs.
4.5 Maintaining emergency preparedness with trained response teams, periodic
drills, and coordination with relevant authorities.
4.6 Reviewing and improving performance through audits, corrective actions, and the
adoption of industry best practices.
5. Health and Safety Risk Management
Saatvik shall identify, assess, and control workplace hazards to prevent injury and ill -
health. The company maintains a structured risk management framework that includes:
5.1 Hazard Identification and Assessment: Saatvik shall conduct periodic formal
Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) and Job Safety Analysis (JSA)
through workplace inspections, incident analyses, and Safety Committee
consultations.
5.2 Control Implementation: Saatvik shall regularly inspect and maintain all
equipment, machinery, and vehicles to ensure safe operation and compliance
with applicable standards. Preventive and protective measures shall follow the
hierarchy of elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, and personal
protective equipment (PPE) controls. These include removal of unsafe tools,
substitution of safer chemicals, strengthening of Standard Operating Procedures
(SOPs), and provision of appropriate PPE such a s flame -resistant clothing and
cut-resistant gloves.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
5.3 Periodic Review: Risk registers and control measures shall be reviewed at least
once every year or following major operational changes. Their effectiveness shall
be evaluated through incident investigations, root cause analyses, and
performance monitoring using defined KP Is such as near misses and incident
frequency rates. Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) shall be implemented
and tracked to closure, and the insights gained shall be incorporated into
management reviews to strengthen Operational Health and Safety (OHS)
practices and maintain compliance with evolving regulations.
6. Emergency Preparedness and Response
Saatvik shall establish and maintain comprehensive emergency preparedness plans to
minimize potential harm during unexpected events. Each site shall:
6.1 Maintain trained Emergency Response Teams (ERTs) equipped to manage fire,
medical, and other crises.
6.2 Conduct mock drills and evacuation exercises at least twice annually.
6.3 Coordinate with local emergency services, fire authorities, and hospitals to
strengthen community -level readiness.
Workers shall have the right to refuse unsafe work in accordance with Saatvik’s Incident
Management Standard Operating Procedure. Such refusal shall be free from any form of
reprisal or discrimination under the company’s grievance and non -retaliation policies.
7. Training and Awareness
Saatvik shall ensure that all employees and contractual workers are competent to
perform their work safely. Training needs shall be identified through risk assessments,
audits, and incident investigations. Induction, daily toolbox talks, and quarterly safe ty
trainings shall be conducted in Hindi and local languages by qualified EHS professionals
and external experts. Programs shall cover fire and electrical safety, chemical handling,
PPE usage, working at heights, machine safety, emergency response, first a id, and
incident reporting. Participation shall be mandatory, free of cost, and conducted during
paid working hours. Training effectiveness shall be evaluated through periodic drills and
on-the-job performance monitoring.

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8. Workforce Health and Well-Being
Saatvik is committed to safeguarding the physical, mental, and emotional wellbeing of
all persons working within or on behalf of the company.
Occupational health services form part of the Integrated Management System and
include health check -ups conducted during employee and worker onboarding, as well
as periodic medical examinations thereafter, workplace hygiene monitoring, and
medical support during emergencies. Qualified medical practitioners conduct these
services, and all health data is stored securely and accessed only by authorized
personnel in accordance with statutory requirements.
Participation in medical examinations shall remain voluntary. Results shall be treated
as confidential and used solely for fitness -for-duty certification. No worker shall be
discriminated against based on medical status, and equal treatment shall be
maintained for all employees and contractual staff.
Saatvik shall facilitate voluntary health -promotion programs such as health camps,
lifestyle awareness sessions, mental well -being programs, and tie -ups with local
healthcare providers, covering both occupational and non -occupational well-being.
9. Grievance Redressal and Corrective Action Plan
Saatvik shall maintain an open, transparent, and responsive mechanism for reporting
health and safety concerns, incidents, and near -misses. All employees, workers,
contractors, and visitors are encouraged to report unsafe acts or conditions through
safety@saatvikgroup.com.
Reports may also be made anonymously or with disclosure through Saatvik’s
Whistleblower and Grievance Mechanism, as disclosed in our Whistleblower Policy ,
that is available on Saatvik’s website . Saatvik shall ensure that every concern raised is
acknowledged, addressed, and documented in a fair and transparent manner.
In addition to email -based reporting mechanisms, workers shall have the option to
directly report unsafe conditions to their respective line in -charge or safety officer. The
contact details of designated safety personnel shall be prominently displayed on s hop-
floor notice boards to ensure accessibility. Saatvik shall implement a Reward and
Recognition Program to encourage proactive identification and reporting of hazards and
near-misses, thereby strengthening a culture of transparency, accountability, and
continuous improvement in workplace safety.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Every reported case shall be acknowledged within 48 hours and investigated within 10
working days to identify the root cause and establish corrective and preventive actions.
The EHS Department shall verify implementation and closure of all actions within 3 0
days, unless otherwise specified for complex cases. Key findings shall be shared across
departments to promote organizational learning and continuous improvement.
10. Product and Customer Health and Safety
Saatvik ensures that its products and services are designed, manufactured, and
delivered with the highest safety standards.
10.1 All solar modules are tested and certified per BIS, IEC, and other global safety
standards.
10.2 Installation manuals include clear handling and electrical safety instructions.
10.3 Customer feedback on safety or product performance is reviewed periodically.
11. Quantitative Commitments
Saatvik shall measure its performance against defined objectives and targets, including:
11.1 A 20% reduction in lost time injury frequency rate (LTIFR) by FY 2028 compared
with the FY 2025 level.
11.2 No more than one lost -time incident per 200,000 working hours.
11.3 Biannual safety audits at all operational facilities.
11.4 100% employee and contractor participation in annual health and safety training
by FY 2028.
11.5 A 20% reduction in product -safety-related warranty complaints by FY 2028
compared with the FY 2025 level.
12. Roles and Responsibilities
Saatvik’s Executive Management shall provide leadership and resources to ensure
effective implementation of this Policy. Heads of Departments shall integrate safety into
daily operations and decision -making. The EHS Department shall manage training,
audits, and compliance with statutory and organizational requirements. All employees
and contractors shall adhere to safety procedures, use prescribed PPE, and report

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
unsafe acts or conditions. Saatvik shall maintain competent EHS professionals across
all sites to monitor and continually improve the Health & Safety Management System.
13. Continual Improvement
Continual improvement under Saatvik’s Integrated Management System shall be
achieved through internal and external audits, management reviews, proactive
monitoring of unsafe acts and conditions, and active worker participation. Findings from
incident inves tigations, risk assessments, and audit outcomes shall be reviewed by
management and the Safety Committees to enhance the effectiveness of occupational
health and safety practices and ensure alignment with emerging national and
international regulations.
14. Worker Participation and Consultation
Formal Health and Safety Committees are established at each plant, comprising
representatives from management, supervisors, and workers, including contractual
staff. These Committees shall meet at least quarterly and as required following
significant incid ents to review safety performance, identify hazards, and recommend
corrective measures. Proceedings of all meetings shall be recorded, communicated to
relevant personnel, and monitored for timely implementation. Saatvik shall protect all
Committee members and participants from any form of reprisal and shall ensure that
all suggestions or concerns raised by workers are acknowledged, reviewed, and acted
upon wherever feasible.
15. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder
expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made i n
writing and will become effective upon approval of the ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The EHS Department of Saatvik is the final
authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy. Saatvik reserves
the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

Human Rights Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and EƯectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is eƯective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
Respect for the human rights is fundamental to the sustainability of any business and
communities in which we operate and also, it is a constitutional right provided to all of
us by the Government of India. Constitution of India provides its citizens the following 6
rights:
a. Right to equality
b. Right to freedom
c. Right against exploitation
d. Right to freedom of religion
e. Culture and educational rights
f. Right to constitutional remedies
2. Objective
2.1. To establish a formal framework demonstrating Saatvik’s commitment to
upholding and implementing its Human Rights Policy (“Policy”).
2.2. To ensure conformance to fundamental labour principles including the
prohibition of child labour, forced labour, freedom of association and right to
collective bargaining and protection from discrimination of any nature.
3. Scope & Applicability
This Policy, titled “Human Rights Policy” (“Policy”), is applicable across operations of
Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik
Group” or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all employees (including directors, o Ưicers, permanent sta Ư,
trainees, probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers,
agents, business partners, and any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or
indirectly, to ensure compliance with the highest standards of corporate governance
and regulatory requirements.
4. Basic Principles and Governance

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Saatvik acknowledges and aligns its practices with the principles outlined in the
following international standards:
4.1. United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
4.2. Applicable labour laws
5. Policy, Procedure & Guidelines
5.1. Saatvik recognises the valuable role that business can play in the longer-term for
the protection of human rights. Saatvik is committed to respecting the human
rights of our workforce, communities and those a Ưected by our operations
wherever we do business (including our contractors and suppliers).
5.2. Our commitment entails respecting human rights and seeking to avoid
involvement in human rights abuses, identifying, assessing and minimising
potential adverse impacts through due diligence and management of issues, and
resolving grievances from a Ưected stakeholders e Ưectively and the Saatvik
endeavours to achieve our commitment by following:
a. Legal Compliance and Due Diligence: Saatvik shall maintain positive
legal compliance with applicable constitutional and regulatory human
rights requirements and align with its Sustainable Business Framework.
Saatvik shall undertake an iterative, due diligence process, the focus of
which is identifying, assessing and managing potential human rights risks
and impacts;
b. Policy Alignment: Saatvik shall align existing policies, processes and
activities with commitment to respect human rights, including those that
apply to labour practices, engagement with indigenous peoples; land
acquisition, supply chain, and security management;
c. Training and Awareness: Saatvik shall promote awareness of human
rights among employees at various levels of operations through training
and communication, engaging with stakeholders in an inclusive,
transparent and culturally appropriate manner on human rights concerns
related to our business activities;
d. Employee Health and Safety: Saatvik shall prioritize the health and safety
of its employees, workers, contractors, and all stakeholders across all
business operations. Saatvik has established comprehensive health and

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
safety management systems, which include regular risk assessments,
safety training, and the provision of personal protective equipment (PPE)
and is dedicated to continuously enhancing its health and safety practices
across all areas. All facilities comply with local and international health
and safety standards, with ongoing monitoring of workplace hazards to
protect well-being;
e. Freedom of Association and Collective Bargaining: Saatvik shall respect
the right of all workers to form, join, and participate in trade unions and
collective bargaining activities of their choice, without fear of intimidation
or reprisal, in accordance with national laws. Engagements with worker
representatives shall be promoted, documented, and non-retaliation
principles shall be strictly upheld;
f. Safe and Healthy Working Conditions: Saatvik shall provide safe working
conditions for employees, customers, business partners, and visitors,
while continuously working to improve safety performance and minimize
risks while promoting awareness and strict adherence to applicable health
and safety laws.
g. Human Rights in Supply Chain: Saatvik shall inﬂuence contractors,
suppliers and other organizations with whom Saatvik has leverage to adopt
Sustainable Business Framework and to encourage and support the
development of equivalent management systems and developing
goodwill, creating sustainable employment and stimulating economic
opportunities in the communities that host our activities;
h. Continuous Improvement: Saatvik shall establish clear accountability by
assigning adequate resources and responsibilities for e Ưective
management of human rights risks; and continually improve human rights
performance by sharing good practices and learning, setting and reviewing
targets, and monitoring, reporting and disclosing performance.
i. Fair Working Hours and Wages: Saatvik shall ensure that employee work
schedules comply with applicable local labour laws governing maximum
working hours and rest periods. Employees shall be entitled to at least one
day of rest within every seven-day period. All overtime work shall be
voluntary and compensated, in accordance with legal requirements.

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Deductions from wages as a form of disciplinary action shall be strictly
prohibited.
6. Restriction and Remedial of Child Labour
Saatvik prohibits and restricts child labour in any of its facilities and is committed to
adhering to all applicable laws, rules, and regulations to prevent any legal anomaly to
ensure the prodigious of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation)
Act, 1986.
Saatvik has a strict policy against the employment of any Child and takes strict action
against any person responsible for the engagement of any Child at Saatvik.
“Child/Children” as used in this policy means any person(s) below the age of 14 years.
Saatvik recognises and upholds international best practices on the prohibition of child
labour, as set out under the International Labour Organization’s Convention 138
(Minimum Age) and Convention 182 (Worst Forms of Child Labour). In India, the
principal law governing the employment of children is the Child and Adolescent Labour
(Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. Under the Act, no child below the age of 14 years
is allowed to be engaged in any occupation or process, and no adolescent below the age
of 18 years is allowed to be engaged in any hazardous occupation or process.
Saatvik is fully compliant with both the applicable provisions of Indian law and the
relevant International Labour Organization conventions.
6.1. Saatvik’s Approach to Prohibition of Child Labour:
a. Saatvik is committed to prohibiting the practice of employing Children. Saatvik
hires only those individuals who have completed at least 18 years of age, on
conﬁrmation of their ages by way of recognized and valid legal documents like
birth certiﬁcate, SSLC marks card, school transfer certiﬁcate, age certiﬁcate
issued by the Employees’ State Insurance medical o Ưicer, driving license, and/or
passport.
b. Prior to engagement with Saatvik, it is mandatory for any applicant to submit one
or more of the recognized legal documents as set out in clause 5.1. Saatvik
undertakes veriﬁcation of the stated credentials by the applicant against the
information provided in the documents. Saatvik does not conduct independent
veriﬁcation to determine the veracity of the document.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
c. While Saatvik takes best e Ưorts to prohibit the employment of Children, it relies
on the information and documents furnished by the candidate to determine the
age of such a candidate. In the event of a candidate falsifying any documents to
appear above the age of 18/14 years, Saatvik shall proceed to terminate the
services of such candidate and may take any action as available to it under law.
d. If any person employed or engaged with Saatvik is found to be soliciting or
facilitating employment of any Child, Saatvik shall take strict disciplinary action
against such person, which may include termination of the services of such
person and reporting to appropriate law enforcement authorities.
e. Saatvik also requires that its suppliers, agents, and contractors commit not to
engage or employ Children. Prior to entering into a relationship with Saatvik, all
suppliers, agents, and contractors are required to execute an undertaking that
they do not engage any Children in respect of their services provided to or on
behalf of Saatvik.
f. Each employee of Saatvik has a duty to comply with the provisions of this Policy.
If any employee of Saatvik has any knowledge of the employment of any Child in
Saatvik or any advertisement of solicitation of Children, he/ she shall
immediately report this to his/her Human Resource Head.
g. Notwithstanding any other provision of this policy, nothing in this policy shall be
applicable to the engagement of any Child by Saatvik, if such engagement is an
internship, and is done after school hours or during vacations, and is with the
consent of his/her parents.
6.2. Compliance with Laws:
a. If any person above the age of 15 years, but below the age of 18 years, is employed
at Saatvik as permitted by applicable law, Saatvik shall undertake all measures
as prescribed under applicable law in respect of employment of such persons,
including in respect of their working hours, overtime hours, weekly holidays, and
their health and safety.
b. Saatvik shall maintain a register in respect of all such individuals as stipulated in
clause 6.2.a, employed by Saatvik, which sets out all the requirements as
stipulated by applicable law.
7. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) & Anti-Discrimination

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Saatvik recognizes diversity, equity, and inclusion as essential to fairness, innovation,
and business success. We are committed to maintaining a workplace where every
individual is respected, valued, and given equal opportunity to thrive. We have a zero-
tolerance stance toward discrimination or harassment and are committed to an
inclusive culture that enables all employees to reach their potential.
This section seeks to ensure that all individuals covered under Saatvik’s policies,
practices, and processes are treated fairly and equitably and are not subjected to less
favorable treatment on the grounds of age, race, religion, creed, color, national origin or
ancestry, physical or mental disability, marital status, gender, gender identity or
expression, sexual orientation, caste, or any other characteristic protected under
applicable law.
7.1. Saatvik’s Commitments:
a. Providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment for all
employees. This applies to all employee-related processes and decisions,
including but not limited to:
i. Recruitment, selection, and career progression
ii. Terms and conditions of employment and compensation
iii. Working environment and health, safety and welfare measures
iv. Training and professional development
v. Redundancy and re-deployment
b. Employing best practices in regard to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI)
initiatives, benchmarked with globally reputed companies and institutes, and
embedding DEI considerations into all HR and business decisions. Saatvik shall
provide an environment of equality, dignity, and mutual respect for all employees
and contractors.
c. Harassment in any form, verbal, physical, psychological, or sexual, is strictly
prohibited, and awareness sessions shall be held annually to prevent such incidents
d. Not discriminating against any individuals based on their gender, age, disability,
ethnicity, sexual orientation, family status, marital status, religious beliefs, caste,
socio-economic background, nationality, or any other protected characteristic.
Saatvik shall operate in accordance with all applicable legislation in the
jurisdictions where it operates.
e. Ensuring fairness and avoiding unlawful discrimination in matters including
recruitment and selection, remuneration, employment terms and conditions,

8
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
promotions, professional development, and performance evaluations. Saatvik
shall conduct periodic reviews of these processes to identify and correct
potential bias and shall promptly and fairly address complaints of harassment,
bullying, or discrimination raised by employees, customers, suppliers, or other
stakeholders.
f. Providing reasonable workplace accommodation for employees with disabilities.
g. Reviewing the Group’s employment policies and practices to promote fairness
and address gender bias and underlying barriers to achieving gender balance,
and to enhance the representation of underrepresented groups, including
persons with disabilities.
h. Building leadership capability by providing equal opportunities for training and
development of sta Ư, as required, to harness their full potential, and providing
equal opportunities for all employees in respect of career progression.
i. Ensuring equal pay for equal work by periodically reviewing compensation
structures to identify and eliminate unjustiﬁed pay gaps.
j. Encouraging suppliers and contractors to uphold equivalent non-discrimination
and inclusion standards within their operations and workforce.
7.2. Policies and Practices:
A range of policies, processes and practices are in place to promote equity, inclusion,
and dignity at work. These include:
a. Dignity at work: Saatvik’s policies are designed to be inclusive of all employees,
irrespective of gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation.
Examples include dress code policy, adoption leave policy, paternity leave policy
and Maternity Leave Policy. We recognize the domestic partner of an employee,
irrespective of their gender, for applicable policies and processes, e.g., the
Mediclaim program.
b. Work-life balance policies: These include a range of ﬂexible working initiatives,
parental leave, and childcare. While every e Ưort will be made to accommodate
requests for ﬂexible/alternative working arrangements, consideration must be
given to business priorities.
c. Prevention of workplace harassment: Saatvik strictly prohibits any form of
workplace harassment, whether physical, psychological, verbal, sexual, or
digital. Managers are responsible for ensuring a professional environment where
all employees feel respected and safe. Awareness sessions on prevention of

9
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
sexual harassment, workplace civility, and respectful communication shall be
conducted annually.
d. Training and awareness: Saatvik shall organize mandatory annual training and
sensitization programs for all employees, including managers and contractual
staƯ, covering topics such as diversity, inclusion, unconscious bias, prevention
of discrimination, and harassment. Specialized training modules shall also be
conducted for recruitment, HR, and supervisory personnel to prevent bias in
hiring and promotion processes. Saatvik aims to ensure 100% coverage of
employees by FY 2027.
e. Supplier inclusion: Saatvik expects its suppliers, contractors, and business
partners to uphold equivalent DEI and anti-discrimination principles.
7.3. Roles & Responsibilities:
a. Saatvik’s Management and Leadership shall lead and support the Company in
creating an inclusive and diverse workplace. They are responsible for ensuring
that eƯective policies and processes are in place to achieve Saatvik’s equity and
diversity objectives. Management shall provide guidance, resources, and
direction for implementing this Policy and advise colleagues on addressing
equity-related matters in the workplace.
b. Managers and Functional Heads are responsible for ensuring that all policies and
processes relating to recruitment, selection, career development, discipline, and
grievance are applied in accordance with statutory requirements and
organizational commitments to promote equity and eliminate discrimination.
They shall also ensure that employees are encouraged and supported to reach
their full potential.
c. Employees are responsible for upholding and implementing the objectives of this
policy and contributing to a safe and inclusive environment that celebrates
diversity.
d. Employees shall refrain from engaging in any conversation, behaviour, or activity
that reﬂects explicit or implicit bias toward any individual or group. Any violation
of this Policy may result in disciplinary action in accordance with company
procedures.
7.4. Board Diversity:
a. Saatvik recognizes that diversity within its Board of Directors is integral to
eƯective governance and sustainable decision-making. A diverse Board brings

10
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
together a balance of skills, perspectives, and experiences that enhance the
quality of oversight and strategic guidance.
b. Saatvik seeks to maintain an appropriate mix of competencies across functional,
industry, and leadership domains, while also promoting diversity in gender, age,
background, and professional expertise. The Board Nomination and
Remuneration Committee shall periodically review the composition of the Board
to ensure that it continues to reﬂect a broad range of perspectives aligned with
Saatvik’s strategic direction and values of inclusivity.
c. Appointments to the Board shall be made through a formal and transparent
process, considering merit, integrity, and the contribution that each candidate
can make to Saatvik’s governance e Ưectiveness and diversity objectives. The
Committee shall also review this Policy periodically and recommend updates to
ensure continued alignment with applicable governance requirements and
leading practices.
7.5. Measurement and Impact:
a. Saatvik’s diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives shall be measured on an
annual basis. Each year, the Board of Directors shall establish speciﬁc objectives
for gender diversity and other priority areas of inclusion identiﬁed by the Board.
b. Saatvik’s current diversity objectives include:
i. Establishing group-level Diversity Councils with deﬁned charters and
agendas;
ii. Achieving agreed-upon diversity hiring targets for both campus and lateral
recruitment; and
iii. Monitoring year-on-year progress in overall workforce diversity across all
levels and functions
c. The following gender diversity indicators have been set for Saatvik and progress
shall be reviewed and reported annually:
i. Percentage of women in senior management
ii. Percentage of women recruited during the year
iii. Percentage of total full-time female employees across Saatvik
d. The Human Resources Department shall compile and review these metrics
annually, report the outcomes to the Board and the Group Diversity Council, and
recommend corrective measures or new initiatives where necessary to support
continual improvement.

11
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
8. Reporting and Grievance Mechanism
8.1. Reporting of Violations:
Employees, workers, contractors, suppliers, agents, business partners and third-party
workers are encouraged to report any suspected instances of bonded labour through
Saatvik’s Whistleblower Policy and Vigil Mechanism, available on Saatvik’s o Ưicial
website.
Reports can be made anonymously. Saatvik has a strict zero-tolerance policy for
retaliation and guarantees protection from retaliation for individuals who report
concerns in good faith
8.2. Reporting of Harassment and DEI Incidents:
Saatvik provides a conﬁdential and accessible mechanism for reporting incidents of
discrimination, harassment, or inequitable treatment. Employees, contractors, or
suppliers may report concerns through Saatvik’s Whistleblower Policy and Vigil
Mechanism, available on Saatvik’s oƯicial website, or directly to the HR Department. All
reports shall be acknowledged within 7 working days and investigated within 30 working
days.
8.3. Investigation and Remediation:
Any reported violation of this Policy will be thoroughly investigated by Saatvik. If a human
rights violation is discovered, immediate corrective action will be taken to address the
situation and provide support to the a Ưected employee.
This may include the provision of ﬁnancial support, legal assistance, and alternative
employment opportunities for the a Ưected individuals.
9. Our Commitments
9.1. Achieve a 20% reduction in Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) by 2027
compared to the baseline year 2025
9.2. Maintain 100% adherence to health and safety regulations at all facilities on an
ongoing basis
9.3. Ensure that all employees have access to clear and transparent two-way
communication channels for raising workplace concerns and sharing
suggestions by FY 2025

12
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
9.4. Conduct annual evaluations of employee pay and beneﬁts to uphold fairness,
equity, and competitiveness in compensation structures
9.5. Encourage and safeguard employees’ freedom of association and collective
bargaining rights in line with applicable labour laws
9.6. Conduct human rights impact assessments on critical operations by FY 2028
9.7. Carry out annual risk-based audits for 50% suppliers by FY 2027, to ensure
adherence to Saatvik’s Human Rights and Supplier Code of Conduct
9.8. Conduct periodic audits covering at least 50% of high-risk suppliers by 2030 to
ensure they are free from child labour practices, with a plan to expand coverage
in subsequent years gradually
9.9. Ensure zero tolerance for child labour across Saatvik’s own operations and
extend compliance requirements to all direct suppliers by 2030
10. Responsibility
The Human Resources department is responsible for developing the human rights
policy and proposing annual objectives to the Board of Directors. It must also identify
best practices and tools that Saatvik can use to help achieve its commitments and
targets.
11. Review and Amendments:
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of signiﬁcant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder
expectations, and legal requirements. Saatvik remains committed to continually
improving the human rights practices. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made in
writing and will become e Ưective upon approval by the ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The Human Resources Department of Saatvik is
the ﬁnal authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy. Saatvik
reserves the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

A1-A3 - Cradle to Gate – Mandatory Module
The product stage of the products is subdivided into 3 modules A1, A2 and A3 respectively “Raw material
supply”, “transport to the manufacturer” and “manufacturing and packaging”. The aggregation of the modules
A1, A2, and A3 is allowed by EN 15804:2012+A2:2019. This rule is applied in this EPD and denoted by A1-A3.
• A1- Raw material supply:
This stage includes extraction and processing of raw materials for the manufacturing of N-TOPCon
Bifacial G12R photovoltaic module. Main materials used in the production are silicon cells, solar glass,
aluminium, back sheet (silica gel, ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA)/polyolefin encapsulant (POE), junction
box (consists of cable, connector and diode), and some minor parts such as plastics and copper.
• A2- Raw Material Transportation
In this module, transportation is considered in the context of the transportation of raw materials to the
production plant and the transportation within the plant. The main mean for transportation of raw materials
is by trucks.
• A3- Manufacturing
Environmental impacts due to the production of N-TOPCon Bifacial G12R photovoltaic module are
considered in this module. Following processes are included: production of high-grade silicon, melting
and ingot forming, wafer production, solar cell production, module production (cutting, taping, soldering,
sheet cutting, mounting and packing) complete the G12R modules.
• A4 – Transportation to the Site
This stage considers transportation of the solar modules to the intended market locations. Main markets
for the PV modules are India and USA. The transportation routes (by container ships and trucks) and the
distances are individually provided by the manufacturer
• A5 – Installation
For this module, waste treatment of packaging materials is considered. It is assumed that no additional
waste is generated during the installation. In addition, considering 1% cut-off rule, the energy needed
during the installation becomes negligible and assumed to be zero. Biogenic balancing for packaging has
been done in A5.
B1 -B7 Use Stage
The use stage is divided into the following modules:
The product has a reference service life of 30 years. This assumes that the product will last in situ with no
requirements for repair, replacement or refurbishment throughout this period. Therefore, it has no impact at this
stage, except for maintenance B2. However, as per cPCR the equations for the user of the EPD to be able to
calculate the total produced electricity for the declared module is given.
• B1: Use
No material or energy inputs, nor any emissions, occur during the use phase at the installation site.
• B2: Maintenance
According to PCR EN 17074, only the maintenance by cleaning glass with water and cleaning
agent is included in this study.

• B3: Repair
Under standard operating conditions, no repair activities are anticipated for the PV module during its
service life.
• B4: Replacement
Replacement of the PV module within the defined reference service life is not expected under normal
operating conditions.
• B5: Refurbishment
Refurbishment of the PV module is not required throughout its operational period.
• B6: Operational energy use
The PV module does not consume any operational energy during use.
• B7: Operational water use
No operational water consumption is associated with the PV module.
Energy production in the first year of operation:
(1) E1 = Srad * A * y * PR * (1- deg)
E1 = Energy produced in the first year of operation, kWh/year
Srad = Site specific annual average solar radiation on module (shadings not included), kWh/kWp/year. The
annual radiation must take into consideration the specific inclination (slope, tilt) and orientation.
A = Area of module, from functional unit (FU), m2 (stated in the EPD).
y = Module yield: electrical power, kWp for standard test conditions (STC) of the module divided by the area of
the module (stated in the EPD).
STC: The ratio is given for standard test conditions: irradiance 1000 W/m2, cell temperature 25 °C, wind speed
1 m/s, AM1.5.
PR = Performance ratio, coefficient for losses.
• Inverter losses
• Temperature losses
• DC cables losses
• AC cables losses
• Shadings
• Losses at weak radiation
• Losses due to dust, snow
• Other Losses
deg = yearly degradation rate (stated in the EPD).
Degradation
If no data is available, a default linear degradation rate of 0.007 (0.7 %) per year shall be applied. Product
specific degradation rate may be used if based on evidence (third-party validated report like DNV or other
similar third-party validated documentation/certificates).
The nameplate capacity of the PV module, as printed in the data sheet, shall be used as the starting point of
the degradation curve. If uncertainties on performance measurements are factored in the performance
tolerance provided on the data sheet, e.g. +2.5 % / -0 %, the nameplate capacity without calculating
uncertainties shall be used.
Energy production second year of operation:
E2 = E1 * (1 - deg)
Energy production n year of operation:
En = E1 * (1 – deg) n-1
Energy production over reference service life of module, assuming linear annual degradation:
𝐸RSL = 𝐸1 ∗ (1 + ∑ n-1RSL-1−1(1 − 𝑑eg)𝑛)
RSL = Reference service life for energy-producing unit, from functional unit (FU), stated in the EPD
n = year of operation

C1 – C4 End of Life Stage
C1 – Deconstruction and Dismantling : The dismantling phase of the solar module involves manual and
mechanical removal from the mounting structure. The overall environmental impact of this stage is minimal
compared to the total life cycle of the product. For Module C1, an energy consumption of approximately 2.6 MJ
per functional unit has been considered, based on the Ecoinvent database. No significant emissions or material
losses occur during this phase.

PRODUCT SUSTAINABILITY ,
LIFE CYCLE & END-OF-LIFE
POLICY
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting held on
11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or replaced by the
Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
Saatvik Green Energy Limited (“Saatvik” or “the Company”) is committed to responsible
product stewardship across the entire life cycle of its solar photovoltaic (PV) modules and
associated components.
As a renewable energy manufacturer, Saatvik recognizes its responsibility not only to enable
decarbonization through clean energy generation but also to minimize environmental impacts
arising from product design, material selection, manufacturing, use, and end-of-life
management.
This Policy establishes an integrated framework covering:
• Product Life Cycle Management
• Eco-Design Principles
• Circular Economy Integration
• Responsible End-of-Life (EOL) Management
2. Objective
The objective of this policy is to:
• Establish a structured framework for managing environmental impacts across the full
product life cycle.
• Integrate life cycle thinking and eco -design principles into product development and
innovation.
• Ensure environmentally sound collection, recycling, and disposal processes at end -
of-life.
• Promote circular economy principles including reuse, recycling, and material
recovery.
• Comply with all applicable regulatory requirements relating to product sustainability
and waste management.
• Support Saatvik’s broader ESG and decarbonization commitments.
3. Scope & Applicability
This Policy, titled “Product Sustainability, Life Cycle & End-of-Life Policy” (“Policy”), applies
across operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred
to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
It covers:
• Product design and development

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Raw material selection and procurement considerations
• Manufacturing and operational efficiency
• Product use and performance phase
• Decommissioning, collection, transport, recycling, and disposal
• Collaboration with suppliers, customers, recyclers, and regulatory bodies
This Policy applies to all employees, contractors, suppliers, channel partners, customers,
recyclers, and other stakeholders involved in product life cycle management.
4. Definitions
• End-of-Life (EOL): The stage at which a product is intended to be discarded,
decommissioned, or removed from service by the user.
• Life Cycle Thinking: Consideration of environmental impacts across all stages of a
product’s life—from raw material extraction to disposal or recycling.
• Eco-Design: Integration of environmental considerations into product design to
improve efficiency, durability, reparability, and recyclability.
• Environmentally Sound Management of Waste: Taking all necessary steps to ensure
that waste is managed in a manner that protects human health and the environment
from adverse effects.
• Circular Economy: An economic model focused on resource efficiency, material
recovery, reuse, refurbishment, and recycling to minimize waste.
5. Product Life Cycle & Eco -Design Policy
Saatvik adopts a life cycle approach in designing and manufacturing its solar PV modules,
including Mono PERC and TOPCon product lines.
The Company evaluates environmental impacts across:
1. Raw material extraction and sourcing
2. Manufacturing and assembly
3. Distribution and logistics
4. Use phase (energy generation)
5. End-of-life treatment and recycling
Particular emphasis is placed on maximizing environmental benefits during the use phase
by enhancing module efficiency and service life.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Saatvik integrates eco-design into product development through:
• Designing for high efficiency and long operational life
• Improving durability and reliability to reduce replacement frequency
• Optimizing material use to reduce resource intensity
• Designing for ease of dismantling and recycling
• Reducing hazardous substances in compliance with applicable regulations (e.g.,
RoHS, REACH)
• Enhancing repairability and material recovery potential
Eco-design considerations are embedded within the New Product Development (NPD)
process.
Saatvik’s PV modules are designed to:
• Generate renewable electricity with zero direct emissions during operation
• Deliver high energy yield per unit area
• Achieve long service life to reduce lifecycle environmental impact per kWh
generated
• Comply with applicable quality, safety, and performance standards
Continuous improvement in module efficiency and reliability forms a core part of the
Company’s sustainability strategy.
Saatvik is committed to measuring and improving product environmental performance
through:
• Conducting Life Cycle Assessments (LCA) for selected product families
• Developing Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs)
• Using LCA findings to inform design optimization and material substitution
• Improving manufacturing processes to reduce embodied carbon

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
• Embed life cycle thinking in product innovation and decision -making
• Enhance resource efficiency and material circularity
• Strengthen transparency in environmental performance reporting
• Conduct LCA and/or EPD for 100% of new major product families by 203 5
• Continuously improve module efficiency and lifetime performance
• Increase recyclability and material recovery potential across product lines
Progress is reviewed periodically under ESG governance frameworks.
6. Product End-of-Life Management
Saatvik is committed to responsible management of solar panels and associated
components at end-of-life, minimizing environmental impact and supporting circular
economy principles.
Saatvik will:
• Establish product return and take-back programs, where feasible
• Collaborate with authorized and certified recyclers
• Promote reuse, refurbishment, recycling, and recovery of critical materials
• Reduce landfill disposal through improved recovery processes
• Ensure compliance with applicable e -waste and waste management regulations
The Company will work with:
• Customers for responsible decommissioning
• Authorized recyclers and waste processors
• Regulatory bodies for compliance and reporting
• Suppliers to improve recyclability and material traceability

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
End-of-life learnings will be fed back into:
• Product redesign
• Material selection
• Manufacturing optimization
• Packaging improvements
This ensures continuous circular improvement.
7. Roles and Responsibilities
• Board / ESG Council: Provide oversight and strategic direction.
• Senior Management : Ensure resource allocation and implementation.
• New Product Development Team: Integrate eco-design and circularity into product
development.
• Sustainability and EHS Teams: Monitor life cycle performance, LCA/EPD activities,
and EOL compliance.
• Sales & Marketing: Communicate sustainability commitments to customers and
stakeholders.
• Employees and Contractors: Comply with applicable waste handling and
environmental procedures.
8. Monitoring and Reporting
Implementation of this Policy is monitored through:
• Product development reviews
• Sustainability performance assessments
• Waste management tracking
• ESG and Sustainability reporting disclosures
Key performance indicators are reviewed periodically by the ESG Council.
9. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or operational
changes, to ensure continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder expectations, and
legal requirements.

7
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Any amendments shall be made in writing and become effective upon approval by the ESG
Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The Sales & NPD Department of Saatvik is
the final authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy.
Saatvik reserves the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

title: Protection of Company Information and Intellectual Property Policy

pages.text:
Protection of Company
Information and Intellectual
Property Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
1. Prologue
The Saatvik Group of Companies (“Saatvik”) is committed to protecting all sensitive and
proprietary information, covering its own data and intellectual property (“IP”) and that
entrusted to us by employees, customers, suppliers, and other business partners . We
uphold confidentiality, integrity, availability, and lawful use of information, and we
respect third-party IP rights in all operations. We also ensure traceability of information
across its lifecycle, maintaining visibility over access, movement, and modifications of
sensitive data.
2. Objective
Saatvik Group ("Saatvik") has adopted this Policy in order to protect its own IP and
minimize the possibility of infringement of IP rights of Saatvik and third parties. This
Policy aims to provide a transparent administrative system for the ownership, control ,
and transfer of the IP created and owned by Saatvik .
Through this Policy, Saatvik aims to:
2.1 Safeguard company and third -party confidential information and IP from
unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
2.2 Ensure responsible, lawful handling of information and IP across their lifecycle.
2.3 Embed simple, risk -based controls, training, and oversight to prevent incidents
and enable rapid response when required.
2.4 Saatvik strives to align its information protection framework with recognized
international standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, thereby reinforcing its
commitment to continual improvement in information security management.
3. Scope of the Policy
This Policy, titled “Protection of C ompany Information and Intellectual Property Policy”
(“Policy”), is applicable across operations of Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its
subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff,
trainees, probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors, suppliers,
agents, business partners, and any other third parties representing Saatvik directly or
indirectly.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4. Policy, Procedure & Guidelines
4.1 Company Information and Intellectual Property
The protection of confidential business information and trade secrets is vital to the
interests and success of Saatvik. Examples of Saatvik's confidential information
include, but are not limited to, the following:
• Customer lists, financial information, pending projects or proposals,
pricing/costing and other employee compensation data; any data or
information relating to business information, strategies, list of present or
potential clients/customers, equipment, software, designs, marketing
plans, pricing information, processes, ideas, inventions (whether
patentable or not), schematics and other technical business, models,
design, product drawings (such as 2 -D drawings or 3 -D models)
performance speci fications, conce pts, progress reports and the like
employed by us in the operation and development of its business or
otherwise.
• Such confidential information may be in writing, or presented
electronically, orally, or visually, in readable form , whether on USB flash
drives, memory cards, cloud-based media, or in any form whatsoever, and
stored in any medium.
• In the course of their work or relationship with Saatvik, employees,
contractors and agents may acquire or have access to confidential
information, and it is a condition of employment or work that employees,
contractors and agents treat this as the propert y of Company (or relevant
customer) and refrain from disclosing it to any unauthorized person(s)
under any circumstances without Saatvik's prior written permission.
• Employees, contractors , and agents shall not disclose, part with
possession of, or remove confidential information, now or at any time in
the future, whether during employment or thereafter at any time, to any
person(s) (except to those authorized by Saatvik).
• Employees, contractors and agents are hereby prohibited from using, for
their own purpose or for any purpose other than for Saatvik's purposes, any
private, confidential or secret information, know -how, writings, records,
notes, letters, drawings, plans or any other data belonging to Saatvik,

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
which may have been obtained or come across by virtue of employment or
other relationship with Saatvik.
• Further, all copyrights, works, inventions, trademarks, trade secrets,
innovations, improvements, developments, methods, know-how, designs,
analyses, drawings, reports, and all similar or related information which
relate to the actual or anticipated busine ss, research and development or
existing or anticipated future products, processes, or services of Saatvik
and which are conceived, developed or made by an employee or
contractor in the course of his/her employment/engagement or on
Saatvik's time or proper ty, whether acting alone or in conjunction with
others are deemed work product or are works "made -for-hire" and belong
to Saatvik.
• Individuals are required to promptly disclose all such work product to
Saatvik, and perform all actions reasonably requested by Saatvik (whether
during the term of employment or thereafter) to establish and confirm
such ownership at the Saatvik's expense ( including, without limitation,
assignments, consents, powers of attorney and other instruments).
• However, inventions that an employee or contractor develops entirely on
his/her own time without using Saatvik's equipment, supplies, facilities are
generally not subject to this Policy.
4.2 Information Handling and Access Control
• All confidential information must be classified and stored according to its
sensitivity.
• Access shall be granted on a strict need -to-know basis and revoked
immediately upon role change or separation.
• Company-approved systems, devices, and encrypted channels must be
used for creating, storing, or transmitting confidential data.
• Records shall be retained for the required duration and securely destroyed
or anonymized once obsolete, ensuring no unauthorized recovery or
disclosure.
• Use of personal email, unlicensed software, or external storage devices for
company data is prohibited.

5
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
4.3 Information Security Risk Assessment
Saatvik shall conduct periodic information security risk assessments to identify
and evaluate key risks, vulnerabilities, and controls. The assessment will cover
critical assets, potential threats, likelihood and impact of incidents, and
mitigation measure s. Results shall inform updates to this Policy and related
procedures.
4.4 Third-Party Information and Due Diligence
Business partners or vendors handling Saatvik data must sign confidentiality
agreements and may be screened for information security and IP -protection
controls.
4.5 Training and Awareness
All employees, contractors, and relevant partners will receive periodic training on
confidentiality, data handling, and intellectual -property protection. Refresher
sessions shall be conducted annually or when major policy changes or incidents
occur. Quick reminders and awareness materials may be circulated regularly to
reinforce good practices.
Saatvik aims to achieve 100% training coverage for all eligible employees each
year by FY 2028.
5. Incident Reporting and Response
Any suspected loss, leak, or misuse of company or third -party information must be
reported immediately to the IT/Information Security Head or through the Whistle-blower
channel.
Saatvik will take prompt and proportionate corrective action whenever a breach or non -
compliance with this Policy is identified.
a. The IT/Information Security Head shall promptly assess the report, contain the
issue, and coordinate with relevant teams to prevent further impact.
b. All incidents will be documented, investigated, and resolved through appropriate
corrective and preventive actions.
c. Where required, affected stakeholders will be informed, and necessary actions
will be taken to strengthen controls and prevent recurrence.
d. Employees, contractors or partners who report a genuine concern or suspected
breach in good faith will be protected from any form of retaliation or adverse
consequence.

6
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
e. Any violation of this Policy will be treated seriously. Employees, contractors, or
partners found to be in breach may face disciplinary action, which may include
suspension, termination of employment or contract, and, where applicable, legal
proceedings under relevant laws. Deliberate misuse of confidential or proprietary
information will be considered gross misconduct.
6. Roles and Responsibilities
Saatvik’s management is responsible for approving and overseeing the implementation
of this Policy and for ensuring that adequate resources are allocated to maintain
effective information protection controls. The IT /Information Security Department shall
maintain and monitor these controls, coordinate incident responses, and lead periodic
training and audits. Department Heads are expected to ensure that all employees within
their teams comply with this Policy and that access to sensitive information is grant ed
strictly on a need -to-know basis. Every employee, contractor, and partner must handle
company and third -party information responsibly, complete assigned trainings, and
promptly report any suspected breaches or misuse of information.
7. Monitoring and Review
Saatvik will regularly monitor and review the effectiveness of this Policy and its related
procedures. The IT/Information Security Head shall conduct an annual review covering
information-security risks, vendor compliance, incident trends, and training completion
rates. Any improvements identified through these reviews will be implemented after
management approval, ensuring continuous enhancement of Saatvik’s information and
intellectual-property protection practices.
8. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or
operational changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder
expectations, and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made i n
writing and will become effective upon approval by ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy shall be implied in addition to all Saatvik's current and future IT and/or Information Security
policies and procedures. The IT /Information Security Department of Saatvik is the final authority in
interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the Policy. Saatvik reserves
the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

Quality Assurance Policy
Version 1.0
Approval and Effectiveness
This Policy was reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors of Saatvik Green Energy Limited during its meeting
held on 11th December 2025. The Policy is effective from the same date and shall remain in force until amended or
replaced by the Board/ ESG Council of Saatvik.

2
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Prologue
Saatvik Group (“Saatvik”) is committed to delivering products and services of the highest quality
while ensuring compliance with all applicable national and international standards, statutory and
regulatory requirements. Quality excellence is central to Saatvik’s business strategy, sustainability
performance, and stakeholder trust.
1. Objective
This Policy aims to:
1.1 To ensure that Saatvik’s products and services consistently meet or exceed customer
expectations.
1.2 To embed quality as an integral part of all processes, supported by risk -based thinking
and continual improvement.
1.3 To comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and international standards relevant
to Saatvik’s operations.
1.4 To drive operational excellence through regular audits, certifications, and process
improvement initiatives.
2. Scope of the Policy
This Policy, titled “Quality Assurance Control” (“Policy”), is applicable across operations of
Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the
“Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
The Policy applies to all employees (including directors, officers, permanent staff, trainees
(except summer interns), probationers, and temporary workers), as well as contractors,
suppliers, agents, business partners, and any other third parties represent ing Saatvik directly
or indirectly.
3. Policy Commitments
Saatvik shall:
3.1 Manufacture and deliver products and services that comply with applicable national
and international standards, including relevant ISO certifications, such as ISO
9001:2015.
3.2 Fully comply with applicable statutory, customer-specific, and regulatory
requirements related to product quality, safety, and performance.

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
3.3 Undertake periodic third-party and internal audits to verify Quality Management
System (QMS) certification compliance and ensure continual improvement .
3.4 Encourage open communication, employee participation, and proactive problem -
solving on all matters affecting quality and customer satisfaction.
3.5 Comply with all applicable product quality, safety, and certification regulations issued
by national and international authorities.
4. Quantitative Commitments
4.1 Achieve and maintain ISO 9001:2015 certification across all manufacturing units
within a couple of years of full-scale operation.
4.2 Conduct periodic third-party audits and half-yearly internal audits to assess QMS
compliance and performance by FY 2026.
5. Training and Awareness
Saatvik shall provide continuous training to employees to enhance their technical knowledge,
operational competence, and awareness of quality standards. Training modules shall include
internal quality controls, customer requirements, and root cause analysi s.
6. Quality Risk Identification and Controls
Saatvik shall regularly identify and assess quality -related risks and opportunities using
structured methodologies such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), six sigma, root
cause analysis, and process control assessments. Risk -based thinking shall be integrated
into process design and product lifecycle management to prevent defects and ensure
consistency. Outcomes of these assessments shall inform updates to the Quality
Management System and employee training needs.
7. Customer Satisfaction and Continuous Improvement
Saatvik shall actively measure and monitor customer satisfaction through feedback forms,
service evaluations, and performance metrics. Results shall be reviewed periodically to
identify improvement opportunities. Corrective actions shall be integrated into the Quality
Management System. Saatvik is committed to continual improvement by leveraging
technology, innovation, and process excellence to enhance product reliability and service
delivery.
8. Reporting and Grievance Mechanism

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Employees, customers, or partners may report quality -related issues, product defects, or
deviations from established standards through Saatvik’s Whistle Blower Policy or Grievance
Redressal Mechanism and Vigil Mechanism , available on Saatvik’s official website or directly
to the Quality Assurance Head. All reports shall be acknowledged within seven (7) working
days and investigated within thirty (30) working days. Corrective actions shall be recorded
and tracked until closure.
9. Roles and Responsibilities
Saatvik’s Managing Director and Executive Management shall provide leadership and
resources for the effective implementation of this Policy. The Quality Assurance (QA)
Department shall maintain and continually improve the Quality Management System,
coordinate audits, and ensure compliance with applicable standards. Department Heads
shall integrate quality control measures into daily operations and ensure corrective and
preventive actions are implemented. All employees and contractors shall uphold quality
standards in their respective functions and report any process deviation, product defect, or
quality concern immediately to the QA Department.
10. Corrective Action Plan
Saatvik shall establish a documented system to analyse root causes of non-conformities and
implement corrective measures. Lessons learned from audits, customer complaints, and
performance reviews shall be used to strengthen process control and prevent recurrence.
11. Review and Amendments
This Policy shall be reviewed annually, or in the event of significant regulatory or operational
changes, to ensure its continued alignment with best practices, stakeholder expectations,
and legal requirements. Any amendments to this Policy shall be made i n writing and will
become effective upon approval by the ESG Council of Saatvik.
Disclaimer:
This Policy supersedes all previous policies or practices in Saatvik. The Quality Assurance Department of
Saatvik is the final authority in interpreting and deploying the clauses, rules, and procedures mentioned in the
Policy. Saatvik reserves the right to modify the Policy from time to time.

Supplier Code of Conduct
Dear Suppliers,
Our Supplier Code of Conduct serves as a guiding framework for all our suppliers (including
their employees and associates) , outlining the key principles and expectations we uphold in
our business relationship. Our company, Saatvik , is a strong follower of business integrity,
ethics, and governance, and has absolutely zero tolerance on unethical business practices.
We expect our Suppliers to conduct their business with utmost integrity, honesty,
transparency, and adhere to all applicable laws & regulations.
Saatvik is committed to environmental sustainability and deeply values ESG principles. We
expect our Suppliers to minimize their environmental impact by implementing sustainable
practices, reducing waste, recycling, and conserving natural resources. We als o encourage
suppliers to practice and contribute to the well-being of society at large and promote cultural
diversity.
The following pages will give a detailed description of the Supplier Code of Conduct, and we
seek your commitment and support in practicing the underlying principles thereof for a
sustainable supply chain ecosystem.
For and on behalf of
Saatvik Group

3
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
INTRODUCTION
Saatvik is a leading module manufacturer in India in terms of operational solar photovoltaic
(“PV”) module manufacturing capacity , dedicated to building a sustainable future driven by a
single mission, i.e., to power a sustainable future through responsible solar innovation.
Our commitment to excellence extends beyond our products . It is embedded in how we
partner throughout our value chain. We believe that our Suppliers are an integral part of our
ecosystem, and we are committed to creating an environment where our Suppliers are
confident that they are treated with respect. This Supplier Code of Conduct (“Supplier Code” ,
“Code”) outlines the mechanism by which the Suppliers should act and communicate with
Saatvik. This Supplier Code applies to Saatvik Green Energy Limited and its subsidiaries
(collectively referred to as the “Saatvik Group” or “Saatvik”).
This Supplier Code is to ensure that all suppliers of Saatvik conduct their operations
responsibly, ethically, and in alignment with Saatvik’s ethics, values , and expectations. The
Supplier Code aims to promote responsible business practices, ensure compliance with
applicable national and international laws and standards , including environmental and health
& safety laws, and protect human rights while safeguarding the welfare of workers.
The Supplier Code is intended to drive continuous improvement by encouraging Suppliers to
establish robust management systems, policies, and reporting frameworks that address
environmental stewardship, fair labour practices, workplace safety, and ethical governance.
This Code is aligned with internationally recognized standards, including the ILO Conventions,
the UN Global Compact Principles, and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
By setting these objectives, Saatvik emphasizes collaboration, accountability, and
transparency with its suppliers. Saatvik believes that a responsible and resilient supply chain
is essential for creating long -term value, managing risks effectively, and co ntributing to a
sustainable future for communities, stakeholders, and the environment.
1. APPLICABILITY
For the purpose of this Supplier Code, the term “Supplier” means suppliers/ service providers/
vendors/ traders/ agents/ consultants/contractors/ third parties , including their employees,
agents, and other representatives, who have a business relationship with and provide, sell,
seek to sell, any kind of goods, services, or manpower to Saatvik.

4
Version: 1.0
Policy Date: 11th December 2025
Saatvik firmly believes in conducting all business transactions with integrity and transparency
and ensures that it is ethical, sincere, and open in all its transactions. We expect our Suppliers
to uphold the values of integrity and ethics in all business dealings.
This Supplier Code is binding on all business interactions and transactions done by Saatvik.
Supplier’s Compliance with this Supplier Code is a mandatory condition for maintaining
business relations with Saatvik, and its adherence will be monitored through audits,
inspections, self-assessments, and due diligence processes.
Saatvik reserves the right to modify the provisions of this Supplier Code as it deems fit, in line
with evolving regulations, changes in compliance programs , or changes in law, rules , or
regulations, or any other applicable laws. In such an event, Saatvik shall update the Supplier
Code on its website. All the Suppliers are bound by such changes and consent to acknowledge
the same.
2. BUSINESS ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE
Saatvik expects all of its Suppliers to uphold the highest standards of ethics, transparency, and
compliance in its operations and dealings with Saatvik. All Suppliers must conduct their
business in accordance with the applicable laws, industry regulations , and international
standards, while ensuring fairness and accountability in all interactions.
We expect our Suppliers to partner with us with integrity and in an ethical manner while
complying with the following:
2.1 Compliance with the Laws of Land
Suppliers shall fully comply with all applicable national and/or local laws and regulations,
treaties, and industry standards, including, but not limited to, those related to labor, health and
safety, and the environment. The Suppliers shall maintain all records of such compliance as
mandated under the applicable laws and provide the same to Saatvik upon request.
Supplier shall comply with sanctions, export controls, and anti-money laundering laws; screen
transactions/parties and report suspicious activity as required.
2.2 Anti-Bribery and Corruption
Saatvik is subject to the relevant anti -bribery and corruption laws applicable in India and as
amended from time to time. The Suppliers should ensure that they comply with the relevant
Anti-Bribery and Corruption laws (“ABC Laws”) in both letter and in spirit. Saatvik has a zero -
tolerance policy with respect to any form bribery and/or corruption. Bribery and corruption are

against our values. Saatvik does not permit such actions, nor do we allow third parties acting
on our behalf, such as agents, consultants, Suppliers and contractors to do any such acts.
Suppliers while dealing with Saatvik shall ensure the following:

• Raise invoices and claims in line with the agreed services and supplies, along with the
supporting documents;
• Perform all business dealings transparently and maintain accurate details of the same in
business books and records;
• Abstain from offering any bribe, kickbacks and/or facilitation payments.
2.3 Conflicts of Interest
This includes situations where the Saatvik employee or director may have an interest of any
kind in the Supplier's business, whether through personal relationships, investments,
directorships or any kind of economic ties with the Supplier. In event of any conflict of interest
arising at the time of empanelment or prior/post/during engagement, Suppliers shall promptly
disclose such situations to Saatvik.
2.4 Whistleblower Protection
We require our suppliers to establish and maintain a reliable, accessible, and secure
mechanism for employees, subcontractors, and business partners to report concerns —
including violations of law, unethical practices, environmental risks, safety hazards,
corruption, or human rights abuses—without fear of retaliation or retribution. This mechanism
must support both anonymous and identified reporting.
All reports must be treated with strict confidentiality. The identity of the whistleblower shall be
protected, and information related to the report shall only be disclosed on a strictly
need‑to‑know basis for investigation purposes. The supplier must prohibit and prevent any
form of retaliation, whether direct or indirect, against individuals who report in good faith.
2.5 Ethical Training and Communication
• Suppliers should periodically conduct comprehensive training on business ethics and
fair competition practices of its employees and personnel. The Supplier should
maintain records of trainings conducted and employees covered.

• Ethical expectations must be communicated clearly through policy documents,
onboarding, workshops, or internal campaigns. The Supplier must demonstrate visible
commitment to upholding ethical standards and appoint individuals responsible for

2.6 Fair Business, Advertisement and Competition
Suppliers shall uphold the standards of fair business practices, advertising and competition.
Suppliers shall not engage in collusive bidding, price fixing, price discrimination, or other unfair
trade practices in violation of applicable antitrust laws.
2.7 Responsible Sourcing
• Suppliers shall avoid sourcing from suppliers or regions that are linked to human rights
abuses, illegal trade, conflict minerals, or modern slavery.
• Suppliers shall conduct due diligence to ensure that raw materials and services are
ethically sourced.
2.8 Data Privacy and Cybersecurity
• Saatvik complies with all applicable data protection laws and contractual
requirements. Saatvik is committed to upholding the highest data protection and
privacy standards with respect to all Supplier data and personally identifiable
information, also referred to as personal data. We expect our Suppliers to adhere to
similar standards when processing such personal data, including sensitive personal
information. Supplier shall comply with local laws of the land when processing such
personal data.
• Suppliers should ensure adequate measures are implemented to address technical
and organizational security measures, data subjects’ rights, transfer of data , and
retention of data, including deletion, while processing personal data owned, controlled,
and managed by the Suppliers.
• Suppliers shall inform Saatvik of any instance of data breach within 48 hours upon
discovery of the same to supplier_reporting@saatvikgroup.com. Supplier is expected
to fully cooperate with Saatvik and provide them with reasonable access to the data
processing facility for conducting investigations into the reported data breach incident.

• Suppliers should ensure that adequate security controls and practices are
implemented and maintained effectively to ensure sufficient protection of confidential
data.
2.9 Quality & Product Responsibility
Suppliers shall ensure that the quality of product/service delivered shall be in line with all the
contract terms and conditions. Suppliers shall adhere to all applicable laws and regulations
regarding the prohibition or restriction of specific substances, including labelling of products,
if required.
2.10 Confidentiality
Suppliers shall ensure that confidential or proprietary information about Saatvik, its clients,
employees or other parties, which has been gained through affiliation with Saatvik or
otherwise, is not used for personal or professional advantage. The confide ntial information
also extends to any employee data, personal data or third -party information as shared by

Suppliers shall take all steps to adhere to the intellectual property rights owned or used by
Saatvik, including but not limited to Saatvik’s copyrights and trademarks.

The Supplier shall ensure that there are plans and procedures to resume business in the event
of any physical disaster (e.g., Such as fire, flood, wind, earthquake, explosion, etc.) or work
stoppage of any kind (e.g., Labor strike, economic/social structur e breakdown, etc.).
2.13 Insider Trading
Saatvik complies with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 ( “PIT
Regulations”). During the course of engagement with Saatvik, if the Supplier becomes aware
of any Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (“UPSI”) relating to Saatvik or any other public
company, the Supplier shall ensure:
• Not to disclose UPSI to anyone inside and/or outside Saatvik , including family and
friends.

either through self or through Portfolio Investment Servicer provider or through
